text:
Elon, before you call what happened in Ukraine a revolution orchestrated by the United States, let me tell you what that story looked like to me—as one person living through it.
I was born in the Soviet Union, in Georgia, and spent my childhood there. Life was poor and limited, but stable: we had electricity, water, heat, food, and security. In 1988, when I was around eighth grade, the Soviet Union began to weaken. National movements were growing stronger in the republics; glasnost and Gorbachev’s reforms had begun. We went to rallies and demanded independence. Georgia gained its independence in 1991. I finished school, and the Soviet Union collapsed.
We believed in freedom and a better future. Reagan and Thatcher were heroes to us; we loved America—Democrats and Republicans alike. We couldn’t tell the difference: right-wing or left-wing—what did it matter to us?! I enrolled in an institute to study business administration, a new field at the time. But soon the lights went out across the country, the gas was cut off, and unrest and civil war began, along with a war waged by separatists backed by Russia. Georgia lost territory. Poverty, corruption, and violence became part of our daily lives. Imagine being 18 to 21, able to study, but with a future that looks uncertain—almost nonexistent.
In the darkened city, here and there, we saw brightly lit offices: generators, heat, computers, internet, and good coffee. Who worked there? Americans. We wanted to get in there too—in the hope of a good salary, prestige, and a better life. Americans funded various programs. Who was behind them? Soros and his foundation. Knowing English and computers opened doors for young people, and the most educated and energetic among us had those skills. Naturally, many young people involved in these programs embraced what we thought were progressive, American, and Western ideas...
Elon, I have a question for you: where were the right-wing and conservative philanthropists then? Ah, yes—the self-satisfied capitalists were busy rolling up their sleeves to cash in on the new Russian markets, weren’t they? Where was the funding for education, scholarships, and civic programs for our part of the world? As a result, the forces that could offer young people real opportunities gained influence over an entire generation’s ideas. Imagine how easy it must have been to influence young people emerging from the Soviet Union—people with no Western education or experience of a free society—when the same ideas gained so much influence even in American universities.
Russia, meanwhile, remained a colonizer and occupier in our region. Let me make one thing clear: saying this does not mean I consider myself a victim or intend to demand reparations. In my view, Georgia did not receive the kind of benefits from Russian rule that classical empires brought to their colonies. Russia was a power with a lower level of culture that conquered a country connected to Western civilization.
Russia’s influence did not disappear with the collapse of the Soviet Union. Through networks inherited from the KGB and through political pressure, it tried to maintain influence over our governments, doing so through the imitation of democratic processes. After the experience of the 2020 and 2026 U.S. elections, the question of how elections can be influenced or stolen should no longer be unfamiliar to you. When people came out to protest this, it was precisely the young people who knew English and computers who took the lead. My question again: where were the right-wing and conservative movements then? Many of them do business with Russia and, in their business dealings, treat Georgia, Ukraine, and other former republics as part of Russia’s sphere.
So when people oppose governments backed by Russia, that does not automatically mean a foreign-orchestrated coup. Sometimes it is a struggle for independence—a country’s attempt to choose its own future.
I am an American citizen today. I always vote for Trump and right-wing forces. In my former homeland, too, I try to spread conservative ideas and fight leftist influence. Elon, when you tell Ukrainians that their protest against a pro-Russian government was not a democratic process, you are telling me the same thing about Georgia’s Rose Revolution. You lump all so-called color revolutions together. That is exactly what makes me angry: with those words, you portray us not as participants in events in our own countries, but as a mass directed by foreign powers. Maybe that is how it looks from the outside, but I have already explained why it looks that way.
Statements like yours do not help people like me, who are trying to popularize right-wing, free-market, pro-American ideas in our former homelands. Center-right philanthropists should invest in educational programs, scholarships, seminars, and civic initiatives that teach and spread these ideas. That is how you build support and persuade people. Antagonizing entire nations and calling them puppets only pushes them away. I hope I have explained why your words made me so angry—and what kind of support people like me actually need.

text:
On May 17, 2020, heavy rain had swollen Hubble Creek in Jackson, Missouri, turning a familiar spot in the city park into a stretch of fast, dangerous water.

Five-year-old Kinsley Stuart was playing near a low-water bridge when the current swept her into an uncovered drainage culvert beneath it. She disappeared under the surface.

Eleven-year-old Aiden Kyle saw her hand reach above the water. He jumped in and grabbed her, but the suction was too strong, and it started pulling him under as well.

His friend Isaiah Randol jumped in next and took hold of Kinsley's hand alongside Aiden. They still could not pull her free. Then Alex Niedbalski and Aiden's brother, Elias Kyle, went into the water too. Together, the four boys fought the current and got Kinsley out.

She was taken to Saint Francis Medical Center, checked over and released without serious injuries.

The next day, Kinsley's mother, Casey Stuart, wanted to thank them. Her family owned Kenny's Flippin' Burgers in Jackson, and she offered the boys free meals there for life. She told them there was no amount of money that could ever be put on what they did.

The full story, with more from the boys and Kinsley's family, is in the first comment.

🤥 Little-known crypto firm tops Trump gala leaderboard as Democrats plan probes

FastX, a crypto firm with ties to Singapore, holds nearly 1.8 million $TRUMP tokens in its main wallet, about two-thirds more than the next entrant, CBS News reports. The firm is promoting a Chinese-language community for the meme coin and has invited followers to submit questions it could put to President Donald Trump at the dinner.

The Nov. 22 gala at Trump’s Virginia golf club offered invitations to as many as 185 entrants based on their token holdings. When the contest closed, 79 of the 130 wallets on the leaderboard had used exchanges that bar US users, suggesting many entrants may be based overseas. The leaderboard lists wallet addresses and usernames.

Senate Democrats have asked how guests are vetted and whether foreign buyers can use the event to gain access to the president. Democrats plan to investigate Trump’s crypto businesses when they take control of Congress in January. A White House official said the dinner was a private event and carried no promise of government action.

text:
Kim Kardashian says she has never once said no when Kanye West asked for the kids, sending them to Saudi Arabia, Italy and Japan, and she still wakes up to tweets saying she kidnapped them.

She says the family has not heard from him in a couple of months. She has written her answer more than once, and she has never posted it.

This is from Call Her Daddy with Alex Cooper. Kardashian and West have four children, and their 2022 divorce settlement set child support at $200,000 a month, according to reports at the time. That number does not come up in the interview.

Cooper asks when Kanye last saw the kids. Kardashian pauses. "Whenever he'll call for them and ask," she says, "it's probably been a couple months since we've heard from him."

What gets to her, she says, is the story online: "there's this narrative that like I keep the kids." She says there have been times she wanted to "show all of these texts," and that she begs for the kids to go and spend time with him.

"I just wake up and there's all these tweets about how I've kidnapped the kids," she says. "And I'm like, it's not a kidnapping. It's a divorce."

She says she sends them "to Saudi Arabia and Italy and Japan and all over the world, every time he asks." Then: "I've never once denied it." When things are "really super unhealthy," she says, she offers her house or a different time, and when he is having a hard time, "he doesn't really want to see the kids a lot."

Then she gives one example, a birthday party. In her telling, his side said his party was at four, so she held hers at noon, "and now you're going online saying" something else. She does not say which birthday it was.

Cooper says Kanye has said "some pretty like horrible things about you as a mother publicly." Kardashian says she has written drafts. "And then I'm just like, what's the point?" Her reason is one line: "My kids are gonna see this."

She says she never talks badly about their dad because "the last thing my kids need is for them to hear it from me." Then she admits: "I wish I did last time. I had a good post ready to go." The family group chat, she says, "read it, approved it."

My takeaway:
Her whole defense is a list: three countries, a party at noon, a post she never sent. She never calls Kanye a bad father, and she never mentions money, even though the $200,000 a month is public. The heaviest line is the quiet one, a couple of months without a call, and she pauses before she says it. Then she admits she wishes she had posted last time, so the silence clearly costs her something. Her reason for staying quiet is the four kids who will read it one day. We only hear her side here, and Kanye has told a very different story in public, so this is her statement, not a verdict.

Is Kim protecting the kids during a hard stretch, or keeping them from their dad? https://t.co/GUbJBKutXL

text:
She asked coyly. Her cheeks were flushed with both her pleasure and the slightly awkward embarrassment that filled her.
‘Ridiculous,’ Nicolas laughed, ‘listen to this…’
‘Do I have to?’
‘Yes, Madam, you do. I just made every effort to please you, now you have to listen to me. It’s called equity, Dr Riesigerschwanz told me all about it. He made it adamantly clear, if I please you, you are obliged to do as I say, that is how relationships work. I don’t know how we are supposed to get married when you don’t even know the basics.’
‘I’m not marrying you, Nic, I told you this. I don’t want to get married. Not to you. Not to Chester. Not to anyone. I have my own plans.’
‘IT SAYS,’ Nicolas bellowed to drown out Allyra’s protests, ‘as she lay in the afterglow, he placed his hands on her body and massaged her skin with the tenderness of a lover smitten. For hours he kneaded her shoulders and back…’ Nicolas snorted, ‘Yes, I can’t be bothered with all that. It seems a little one sided too. In fairness, if anyone should be massaging anyone, then it should be you massaging me for my astounding performance or at least giving me some money.’

Allyra’s jaw dropped in response to Nicolas’s magnanimous monologue,
‘That is a little insulting, Nic.’
Nicolas ignored her and parked his regal behind in his chair,
‘Aftercare, what absolute nonsense. I am a busy man, I don’t have to be a voluntary physiotherapist, no matter what strange woman ideas you have about it.’
‘I never mentioned it,’ Allyra sighed, ‘you brought all this up when, literally, no one asked!’
‘Next you will want jewellery and chocolates. I have seen you sniffing around the chocolate eclairs in the Sapari bakery, and flowers, you will want them too. I shall be inundated with bees. Then you will ask me to move furniture around only to have me move it all back the next day. You will probably want scented candles delivered daily. Then it will be, Nicolas would you love me if I was a slug? And all that entrapment, before you know it, Corax will be a Tupperware shop filled with free women who all hate me. No, this won’t do. I don’t think I should marry you at all, not with this attitude.’
‘Good, don’t,’ Allyra snapped.
Nicolas pursed his lips, twitched and snorted again,
‘Worry nor, fair maiden, for I shall overlook these failures that saturate my queen’s troubled heart.’

Allyra contemplated asking him again why he spoke in such a weird way, but guessed he would just misfire again or talk more gibberish, and she could not be bothered with either,
‘So, what happens now?’
‘Now? Past. Present and future, or just present?’
‘Any.’
Nicolas cleared his throat, which was a tad slimy,
‘A raven shall carry you yonder and a friend and a stranger shall seduce you as one does when one is one, then you shall drown in my oblivion, marry me as you promised, and lock yourself in a birdcage.’
Allyra waved her hand,
‘Never mind. May I leave?’
‘Indeed, I must prepare for our date tonight.’
‘Whatever you say, Nic.’
‘That’s the spirit,’ Nicolas grinned, ‘now you wish to go to the Sapari Tavern?’
‘I do.’
‘I will hear that again within three moons,’ Nicolas smirked.
‘I’m sure you hear it all the time.’
Nicolas’s mouth opened again, astonished by Allyra’s intuitive mind,
‘Madam, you are correct. Have you ever been told that you must be psychic?’

Allyra had given up talking and let Nicolas continue,
‘We must, unfortunately, delay your movement to enable our good self, the Pied Piper, to pork his way through the sands of Neferaten. I sense that matters are not going his way and it will take him longer than one usually takes to deliver the post!’
Allyra shook out her hands,
‘I am supposed to meet Chester after his shift.’
‘He’s running late,’ Nicolas snapped, ‘I just told you this.’
‘How would you know?’
Nicolas’s eyes shifted from side to side,
‘Would you do me a service, Immoless?’
‘What?’
‘I should like you to sit in my chair, just stand and I shall move, and then you sit.’
Allyra tutted,
‘I’m not a dog.’
Nicolas’s face dropped, and he made every effort to look hurt,
‘Please, humour me!’

Nicolas stood and allowed Allyra to sit, albeit uncomfortably and a little suspiciously, in his chair.
‘Excellent,’ Nicolas smiled, ‘it suits you, Immoless.’ He moved his face in front of hers. His eyes flashed bright green. Allyra’s eyes whitened in response.
‘Time, time, time.’ Nicolas murmured, ‘You can wait there quietly until Ches returns. When you wake you shall be convinced that you chose to stay and we had a very romantic dinner together.’ Nicolas clicked his fingers, and Allyra’s eyes closed completely.

Nicolas took out his pocket watch and watched as each second ticked by. Every clock in Sapari stopped. Every watch stopped and Nicolas remained still for hours.

Eventually Webster appeared in the glass of Nicolas’s pocket watch,
‘I am pleased to inform you that Chester’s day was most successful. Cedric, Ledgerly and Pauley have assisted. Chester has dined, changed, and is on his way to Sapari as I speak.’
‘Excellent,’ Nicolas said.

The clocks resumed their movements.

Nicolas clicked his finger in Allyra’s face,
‘Did you enjoy your dinner, Immoless?’ He asked.
‘Yes, thank you, I,’ Allyra hesitated, ‘actually no, I…’
Nicolas opted to ignore the glitch and interrupted,
‘Now, we must depart. I shall escort you to the tavern, and you shall reward me with a kiss, to show everyone who you belong to.’
‘I can escort my…’ Allyra’s protest was cut short.

Nicolas pulled her from the chair, dragged her to the window and dropped the two of them into a crouching position. Intestines spewed about Allyra, then a pulsating heart, followed by a liver and bone. Then came muscle, flesh and skin, and finally feathers smoothly formed around them. Instinctively Allyra clung to Nicolas,
‘What’s happening?’ She asked, her voice muffled by the raven’s body that smothered her.
‘I’m taking you where you wish to go.’

The raven that engulfed Allyra and Nicolas trotted about the floor, then took flight, darting through the window and shooting backwards into the sky as lightening kissed its bleak beak. The bird soared, circled Sapari an unnecessary amount of times, and landed outside of the tavern. The feathers retracted first, then the skin, flesh, bone and organs until Allyra was left on the quayside vomiting in Nicolas’s arms. Nicolas was extremely flattered by Allyra’s digestive offerings and held her close to him. He wiped her mouth with his sleeve, declared that he would never wash the love offerings from his suit or indeed ever wash his suit again, then stood her up. Allyra dizzied and fell, but Nicolas caught her,
‘Is that your first flight?’
Allyra nodded, then fell again enabling Nicolas to catch her again. This pleased Nicolas. He pushed his shoulders back, and spoke with a deeper voice,
‘You are saved, my queen.’
Allyra did not answer but talk of the scene quickly drifted through the sprawling gossip train taking the story of Nicolas and Allyra’s torrid love affair from the outside of the tavern to the inside of the tavern, and Banshee came out for a nose.

Nicolas grabbed Allyra and swung her backwards over his arm, lowered her body, and shoved his face into hers,
‘Alas, my queen, I must depart and prepare for tonight,’ Nicolas said as loudly as possible, then pulled Allyra up, grabbed both of her shoulders firmly and plunged his tongue deep into her throat, whilst allowing his lips to grind against hers. His body found itself grinding against her as well. Allyra did not find his lips as offensive as she initially thought, indeed, Nicolas was growing on her. Her own mouth responded to him. Nicolas then stepped back, bowed and sunk into the raven before departing.

Scene VIII: The Hobnailed Boot

The 2ndDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Sapari

Once the raven disappeared into the dusk, Banshee, who had been staring along with the other nosey parkers, scurried up to Allyra and placed an arm about her shoulder,
‘Honey, am I imagining things or was that…?’
‘Nicolas DeSilva,’ Allyra replied.
‘I didn’t know you knew each other, you never told me.’
Banshee brushed the hair from Allyra’s eyes and glared at the blood, ‘Did he hurt you?’
Allyra shook her head.
‘But the blood?’
‘It’s his blood. He vomited on me and I don’t really know him. He has just been following me around for two days.’
Banshee laughed,
‘You could have fooled me! I saw the white stain on his trousers. Looked fresh too. You nasty!’
Allyra shook her head and wiped the vomit from her clothes. The vomit did not want to depart as it had fallen in love with the blood, and the two started to mingle quite happily. Allyra looked Banshee in the eye,
‘I don’t know him. I don’t know him. I don’t know him. I don’t know him. He has been following me around all day.’

Banshee looked Allyra up and down,
‘Calm yourself, Lyra. You have a meeting with Lord Fuckwad soon, you can’t go like that. Jump in the sea, then we can have a look at your makeup.’
Allyra dropped her kleptobag from her back, and handed it to Banshee,
‘Good idea.’ She kicked off her boots, walked to the quayside edge and jumped into the harbour. The cool water raised her spirits, and she rolled underneath its embrace. For a moment, she fancied that she saw the green-locked monster of her dreams watching her, then he was gone. The salt licked her lips. She swam about for short while, then made her way to the steps and climbed back up onto the quayside.
‘That’s much better,’ Banshee smiled as Allyra forced her boots back onto her sodden feet, ‘come.’
They entered the tavern, bypassing Nedi and Chester who were playing poker, and went straight to the ladies’ room. Banshee handed Allyra her bag and watched as Allyra used paper towels and cosmetics to tidy up her face.
‘I suggest you go to the room an hour early, use a sheet to dry yourself and prepare.’ Banshee advised.
‘I need to see Ches first.’
Banshee nodded in agreement; she knew better than to intercede on Chester’s behalf regarding any matter. Once Allyra looked a little more reasonable, both ladies exited the washroom and moved through the growing crowd to the corner booth where Chester and Nedi sat.

Banshee sat next to her beloved Nedi, and Allyra slid in next to Chester. Chester immediately threw his arms about her and held her in a lovingly tight grip,
‘I hear Hector pulled you from the sea again, Lyra,’ he purred, kissing her head, ‘I do worry about you.’
‘I know you do, Ches, but you really don’t need to.’
‘I will always worry about you.’ The Cat said, brushing his face up against Allyra as he let out a deep guttural purr, ‘You’re the best thing that ever happened to me. I couldn’t bear to lose you.’
Allyra laughed and touched his nose,
‘You always say that.’
‘And I mean it.’

Allyra reached for the drink Chester had had specially prepared for her. It was a dark red and green wispy cocktail. Chester insisted on ordering all of her drinks and had them made exactly to her taste. He even added a special serum that Allyra did not need to know about. Allyra took a sip before speaking again,
‘I dunno Ches. It’s been five years and I still don’t know where you live.’
‘Oh. That.’ Chester said, rubbing his head against her shoulder, ‘I’m always here for you, Lyra, you know that.’
‘That’s not the point, is it? Do you know I received an offer of marriage today? And yesterday! I’m not getting any younger, even though I will probably be dead soon, so I might just decide to accept the proposal!’ Allyra joked, even though she did not find the matter funny. Chester cupped her face in his hands and a gigantic smile spread from cheek to cheek,
‘One day soon, I shall take you home and marry you. That’s a promise.’
‘Mmm hmm,’ Allyra nodded, ‘I will be dead soon, Ches.’

Before the conversation shifted from tetchy humour to awkwardness, two gentlemen joined them. One was tall and muscular with a reddish beard, flaxen hair and grey eyes, and the other was tanned with very dark hair and eyes to match.
‘John, Jaeli,’ Chester nodded.
Allyra turned to the muscular man,
‘Can I get you a drink, John?’ Then shifted her gaze to Jaeli, ‘Jaeli?’
‘We would never ask a lady to buy,’ both said in unison. The brothers were a permanent fixture at the tavern, a necessity since they owned the establishment.

Other than Charmaine, who was off sick, all of the bartenders were male as, in 1531 P.V. John and Jaeli’s barmaids kept taking it upon themselves to disappear. At first their staff turnover saw the absence of two barmaids a moon, but this escalated to two barmaids a week.

The locals, being conspiracy nuts, put about a rumour that John and Jaeli were killing them and selling their body parts to the medical department at the Sapari university. However, John and Jaeli took a holiday to Neferaten, and the disappearances continued in their absence. Shortly after, a second rumour gained momentum. One that accused the great Nicolas DeSilva of declaring the women insane and stealing them away to Corax for lunch. Not lunch as in a date, but for his lunch.

The rumour was started by one Snoddle Copperbowl, a stout man whose puffy, purple face, oversized nose, and balding head informed the world that he was quite the brandy drinker. Mr Copperbowl made the heinous claim that he had seen DeSilva ‘Loitering about the quayside’ on the night that two of the barmaids went missing. Nicolas could not decide whether to take Copperbowl to court for misinformation or disinformation. Ledgerly let it be known, via a series of leaks, that both these issues were an ongoing problem in the Deep, as was tickturdery. After much deliberation, Nicolas further decided that both words; disinformation and misinformation had no meaning at all, and Mr Copperbowl just happened to have a nasty accident with a set of secateurs which culminated in him cutting his own head clean off.

The rumours were never mentioned again, and John and Jaeli retained Charmaine, the last living barmaid, and thereafter decided only to hire unpleasant looking, male bartenders.

It had occurred to John and Jaeli that, of late, Charmaine was not looking her best anyway.

‘Shall I deal you in?’ Chester asked the brothers.
‘Do,’ John replied, ‘what are the stakes?’
‘A night with Allyra!’
‘Fuck off with that!’ Allyra snapped.
‘Joking,’ Chester smiled, ‘let’s start at one hundred ardents.’
Chester shuffled the cards, fanning them, flailing them, bouncing them, and generally showing off as much as possible, then dealt everyone a hand.
‘Raise,’ Allyra and Chester said unanimously.
Nedi pulled on his beard,
‘I’m out.’
‘Banshee?’ Chester asked.
‘Raise.’
‘Jaeli?’
‘Raise.’
‘John?’
‘I’m out.’

Chester twiddled his hair,
‘Five hundred ardents.’
Allyra side-eyed him,
‘Six hundred.’
Jaeli looked form Allyra to Chester,
‘Forget it. I’m…’
Before Jaeli could finish his sentence, Chester’s nose inhaled sharply and he noted a change in the air. He rose, forcing Allyra to step out of the booth, and wandered about the tavern sniffing.
‘That’s gross,’ Banshee mumbled.
‘It’s just Ches.’ Allyra said as she watched him approach two red heads. Allyra lowered her eyes. Chester spoke to the ladies for a few minutes, then the two women stood and followed The Cat up the stairs.

Allyra turned over Chester’s cards revealing a royal flush,
‘That cheating rat!’
‘I don’t know why you put up with it!’ Banshee snapped.
Allyra slapped her own royal flush on the table,
‘I mean the cards. The other business doesn’t bother me.’
John shook his head,
‘It should.’
Allyra swallowed her drink in one go,
‘It doesn’t. We have an arrangement. Speaking of which, John, can I have my room key?’
John reached into his fawn suit pocket, pulled out a key and chucked it to Allyra who failed to catch it and had to go crawling about the floor to retrieve it. Once the key was in hand, she stood triumphantly,
‘Enjoy your game!’ She smiled and headed up the stairs.
Banshee and Nedi looked at each other but said nothing.

The room assigned to Allyra was fairly small. Lord Fuckwad did not come for the room. He came for the Allyra experience, and she was experienced. It was the sort of experience that loosened men’s tongues, and at times, their wallets. There was a small bed, which was a little too close to the window. It held a heap of fresh sheets and blankets that were tightly tucked under the mattress. Jaeli and John had been taught by their grandma, May, how to make a bed as difficult to navigate as possible.

May insisted on a bottom sheet, an under sheet, a duvet, a heap of blankets and a quilt. Allyra chose a blanket, stripped off and dried herself. She could hear the ladies that Chester had commandeered moaning in the next room and making an unnecessarily loud and irritating amount of noise.

Dressing again seemed a little pointless as Lord Fuckwad preferred her out of her clothes, so Allyra climbed into the bed and waited, and waited, and waited, until sleep took her.

She was crudely awakened, almost immediately, by a clonk on the head. Then another. Her body jumped and her eyes opened. The curtains were drawn, but the silhouette standing in the darkness seemed much taller than Lord Fuckwad,
‘What happened?’ Allyra asked.
‘You’re late, that is what happened.’
Allyra instantly recognised the deep voice and pulled one of the curtains enough to shed light on the situation. Nicolas stood before her. The dark glasses and fake moustache had made quite the comeback, and his cane, the tool with which he had awakened her, shimmered in the dusk glow.
‘I’m not late. Nicolas, why are you here?’
‘I am not Nicolas,’ Nicolas replied as he loomed over her, ‘I am Lord Fuckwad, now you have to fuck me.’
‘You are Nicolas, I am not fucking you, and where is the real Lord Fuckwad?’
‘I am Lord Fuckwad, but, alas, my predecessor met with a lonely ram who was so melancholy that he removed his heart with a slice of cucumber.’
‘Go away Nicolas,’ Allyra sighed.

‘Would you like me to depart and never return?’ Nicolas asked.
‘That would be nice.’
Nicolas laughed,
‘You jest, Madam. Such an adorable sense of humour.’
‘Nicolas!’ Allyra snapped, ‘Where is Lord Fuckwad?’
Nicolas removed his hat and placed it over his chest,
‘There was an incident. A horrific incident. After the removal of Lord Fuckwad’s heart he grew hysterical and drowned himself in the bilge of your ship, Madam, the Sombre. Quite grotesque it was. Fear not, the rats were so sympathetic to his plight that what they did not eat they shared with the sharks.’
‘So, you killed him?’
Nicolas sucked in a double breath of air,
‘Me, Madam? I could not harm a fly.’
Allyra ignored the performance and took another path,
‘How did you know I would be here? Are you spying on me?’

Nicolas leaned further forward and pressed his hands into Allyra’s thighs,
‘I was not tracking you. The passionate cries from the next room summoned me, and I indulged as your Cat did. It was a sight, the four of us. Your gentleman has no morals, none at all. You should see what he does with…’
‘No thank you,’ Allyra snapped, ‘that’s quite enough of that. I don’t believe you anyway. You keep making up rubbish.’
‘No lie has left my mouth, and I am wounded by such an allegation. Poor Nicolas, broken hearted yet again by your callous words.’
‘You are tiring is what you are.’
‘Thank you,’ Nicolas replied, whilst squelching his hat back into his greasy hair. ‘When I am your Lord and Master, I shall be faithful and merciful.’
‘Will you now?’ Allyra sighed.
‘Probably not,’ Nicolas’s hands reached up to his hat as it tried to escape from his sweaty head, and belted it firmly into place, ‘we shall marry at the Dokeshi Carnival, both times.’
Allyra remembered that she was naked, and shuffled under the sheets,
‘I’m not interested, and you are just talking for the sake of talking.’

Nicolas stared at Allyra,
‘You are naked, aren’t you? Such a welcome indeed.’
Allyra nodded towards the pile of clothes that lay on the floor,
‘Can I have my clothes?’
‘You probably can since they are yours, but they are not yours really, are they?’
Allyra clenched her fists and growled through her teeth,
‘Nicolas give me my clothes.’
‘I would rather not.’
‘And why not?’
Nicolas clonked her on the head with his cane again,
‘One does not talk back to one’s Master.’
‘I think I will come to Corax and commit myself, then you can just eat me and all this will be over with.’
Nicolas licked his lips,
‘I will be eating part of you later tonight.’
A pillow hurtled through the air and smacked Nicolas between the eyes,
‘Vulgar man!’ Allyra barked.
‘I am not a man; I am a demonic-God. Or just a god, and you were the one spreading yourself around my visage not a few hours ago. Encouragement indeed.’
‘You’re a pain in the ass, Nic!’

Nicolas grabbed Allyra’s foot from under the covers and dragged both Allyra and the blankets into his body,
‘You compliment me so beautifully, such poetic words.’
Allyra stifled an exhausted yawn,
‘Why are you doing this to me?’
‘It is a common fact that a gentleman must court a lady before the nuptial contracts are signed. It is good etiquette.’
Allyra placed her hand on Nicolas’s cheek, and stroked his face,
‘I want you to listen to me, Nic. We are not a couple. We are not getting married. My job is to pretend to slay you, your job is to execute me, that is how it goes.’
‘I think I was right, you know? A burgundy wedding dress to go with your hair.’

‘NICOLAS!’ Allyra shouted, but she wasn’t getting through.
‘And perhaps I will take you for your fitting,’ Nicolas continued. He then pulled a notebook and pencil from his inside pocket and scribbled down his thoughts. Allyra waited until he had finished and his ridiculous notebook had been returned to its home before bothering to speak again,
‘Are you happy now? And will you leave so that I can get dressed? As is a matter of gentlemanly decency.’
‘I am very happy, my love,’ Nicolas said, and he was happy, ‘but alas I cannot leave as whilst you were sleeping, I accidentally nailed my feet to the floor.’
‘Your nonsense has lost me a day of reconnaissance,’ Allyra moaned.
‘You do not need to torture my vampires further; I shall impart any Immortalis information you want as now is the time. Your wish is my command.’
Allyra looked at her poor clothes crying in the corner,
‘I wish you to leave.’
‘I already said that my feet are nailed to the floor. I cannot move.’

Allyra pulled away from Nicolas and clambered up the bed, dragging the blankets with her for the sake of modesty. She pulled the curtain open a little further to allow more light in, then crawled back down the bed to Nicolas and peered over the edge. His feet were indeed nailed to the floor. The nails had been tapped through his boots in bulk, and there was a puddle of blood running about the wood below. Allyra tutted, climbed out of the bed, and got dressed, giving Nicolas a very pleasing eyeful. She then threw her kleptobag on her back and headed to the door.
‘Nicolas’s feet hurt,’ Nicolas muttered, ‘please help him.’
Allyra stopped short of reaching for the door handle, sighed, and returned to her monstrous nemesis,
‘Fine. I will help you, then you leave me alone.’
Nicolas did not answer. Allyra picked up the claw hammer that Nicolas had left conveniently close to his boot, knelt down, and started tugging the annoyed nails from his feet.

‘I was thinking,’ Nicolas continued as he watched his bride build a pile of iron, ‘we could honeymoon on Sihr, since you like it so much. I know Elyas well, he’s an atrocious narcissist so he will probably allow it. He likes Monopoly, but you can’t play. I can play because I submitted my resume. I could draw a resume up for you, and then you can play too. I get the boot of course, and Elyas must lose. None of us let him win. Not even Robert, although Robert cheats. Elyas says Robert is dense, and I happen to agree, what do you think?’

Allyra stopped momentarily and looked up at Nicolas as one boot was released from its bondage. Nicolas knelt down next to her, did not wait for a response, and resumed his speech,
‘His name isn’t Theaten, of course, it’s Robert.’
‘His name is Theaten, and you know it’s Theaten.’ Allyra replied.
‘You are mistaken. Of course, His mother thinks his name is Theaten too, but I know better. He says it’s not, but that’s exactly what a Robert would say. He forgot his name when he started hanging around Count Pompous and his slut. Are you a fan of Count Pompous? I doubt it, no one is really. Undeserved gifts were bestowed I am afraid. Sad times. When I bestow gifts upon you, they shall be deserved, but you won’t like them. Robert would have been better off with Anne. Anne and Pompous’s marriage is an abomination, and it only gives Count Pompous fuel for his unwarranted arrogance.’

Allyra continued to pull at the nails, and Nicolas made it as difficult as possible by fidgeting.
‘He lies about me, you know? He tells the most atrocious stories to my brother, then I am inundated with Robert’s hideous company. You will meet Robert before the wedding.

text:
Nicolas coughed again,
‘Forgive me, Madam, I forget that the lower classes have suffered from the ailments of a Thesapien education system. Let me use simple language, will you offer your chirograph in support of the abolition of pomposity.’
Allyra’s eyes twitched,
‘Why are you talking like that? Are you mad or something?’

Nicolas’s moustache dropped,
‘No, Madam, I am not mad.’
Allyra looked closely at his features, and the ridiculousness of his attire,
‘Nicolas DeSilva, Captain Quickdraw! You again!’
Nicolas shook his head, and his moustache drifted further south. He readjusted it before replying,
‘I know of no DeServer, I am Pope Costas Toomuchas Millipedas the Ninth of the great Toadstool-Licking brethren.’
Allyra let out a sigh,
‘You are not. You are Nicolas DeSilva.’
Nicolas leaned uncomfortably close to her face,
‘If I was he, you would be on your knees calling me Master or My Lord.’
Allyra, unmoved by his proximity, lowered her gaze to the seaweed and Ashurrel leaf butts that soiled the quayside,
‘Not in that filth I wouldn’t be,’ she said and reached for Nicolas’s glasses as she spoke, causing him to jump back,
‘Madam, touch not the great sacred being.’
‘I don’t know what you are on about, and I am pretty sure you don’t know what you are on about either. Why are you here, Nic?’

Both Nicolas and Allyra went silent, surprised by her ongoing overfamiliarity. Nicolas spent the brief silence considering what nonsense to talk about next, but the truth bit him before he could spin a silly lie,
‘I am courting.’
Allyra snorted,
‘Not in those clothes you’re not.’
Nicolas jumped into her personal space and grabbed her right arm above the elbow, his cane pressed into her flesh,
‘Madam Immoless, if I were Nicolas DeSilva, which I am not, but if I were do you think it prudent to speak to me in such a disrespectful way?’
Allyra shrugged,
‘It doesn’t make a difference, does it? I know what I was bred for, I’m at peace with it.’ She shuddered as she spoke, and Nicolas released her arm. His head tilted to one side and then the other. Nicolas released both the sign and his cane from his grip, and both stood in position as if held by some magical spell.

Nicolas stepped even closer to Allyra and dropped his head so that his nose touched hers. His arms rose and his hands moved over her curves, almost caressing her body. He sniffed her, then allowed his tongue to stroke her lips, which tingled and swelled in response to his affections. Her breathing deepened.

Nicolas’s tongue retracted and his lips took their place. It was not a kiss, not exactly, but a touch, mouth to mouth. Allyra shivered, then Nicolas’s hands grasped the tops of her arms. His grip tightened and he trembled as if forcibly holding some inner demon at bay. Their lips parted. Nicolas twitched and circled his head. He relinquished his grasp, with some struggle, pushed Allyra away and clenched his fists.

Nicolas twitched again, then forced a smile,
‘Don’t you have a meeting to attend, Immoless?’
Allyra turned from him, still slightly stupefied, went to board the ship, then stopped,
‘Out of curiosity, who are you courting?’ She asked.
Nicolas smirked,
‘Why, you, Madam!’
‘Well, you’re not!’
‘Oh yes I am, our marriage is nigh and actions must be taken!’ Nicolas took a copy of Fanu’s The Busty Bride from his inside pocket, scanned a few pages and selected a beautiful passage to read aloud, ‘The bride responded to his ardent gaze, the touch of his lips, the long, thick, hard, bulbous lump in his trousers that pressed achingly towards her sordid and wet…’
Allyra walked onto the gangplank,
‘Goodbye, Nic. Nice to meet you again, I’m sure.’

The Shipwreck Solis
The Pauci Electi Headquarters
Sapari Port

The Pauci Electi met every fourth day in the shipwreck Solis. Sometimes they met more often just to drink and gamble, and sometimes, as most priests do, they met in the whorehouse above The Sapari Tavern for a ‘field trip.’

When baptised, Pater Solis elected to take the ship’s name. He believed that he was heading an armada, and rumour had it that he was a fundamentalist, but fundamentalist of what no one knew, so no one listened to the pointless gossip. Solis had not actually decided the full nature of his fundamentalism, so there was really nothing to know anyway. He represented Sapari, and each of his congregation represented one area of the Deep to include; the six villages of the Kingdom of Tepes as well as the kingdoms of Bratsioca, Togaduine, Neferaten, Ard Quahila and D’Aten. Both the Electi and the DarkBadb Brotherhood consisted of thirteen stuffy and highly bureaucratic old men. Irkalla also had a board of thirteen to ensure balance when the three groups, The Troika, met. In an emergency, only key representatives of each group were obliged to attend as assembling thirty-nine old men in a short space of time proved highly problematic on account of their nap times and bladder diversions.

The Solis was rotting. No one took it upon themselves to scrub the decks or maintain what was left of her in anyway. Staff turnover was high on account of Nicolas being a jackass, and whenever upkeep was mentioned, the matter was deferred to the next meeting. Before The War Before the Dusk the Electi were stationed in Castle Tepes, but Theaten had claimed the palace and awarded the title and lands to Count Tepes, otherwise known as Roger or Count Pompous.

The Electi meeting would always take place in the galley, and whiskey was served. Afterwards the decrepit gentlemen would engage in poker. Nicolas knew where the Electi headquarters was, after all, it’s not difficult to miss a load of decrepit, cloaked old men struggling to climb aboard an even more decrepit schooner.

During the humid spring of 1532 P.V. Nicolas had released plague-carrying rats onto the ship. He did not want to destroy the Electi, indeed he found their presence amusing. He just wanted to see what would happen. His escapade was almost interrupted by a nosey Immoless wearing a black suit, but Nicolas and Archie managed to redirect her trajectory back to Thanata.

Unfortunately, for Tepes, who governed the kingdom, the rats escaped the ship and terrorised Sapari. Carts had to be brought in to wheel out the dead, and the Immortalis and vampire livestock plummeted. No one wanted a thesapien meal covered in buboes. The lords complained to Tepes, and Tepes complained extensively to Theaten. Theaten visited Nicolas personally to request that he resolve the matter. Nicolas, in response, dispatched Chives to the sands of Neferaten to acquire over one thousand cats. This odyssey required a caravan of carriages and a great deal of injury to Chives and his porters on account of the cats not wishing to migrate from the warm sandy tropics to the perpetual rain of Sapari. Nonetheless, the cats were released in Sapari, whether they liked it or not, where they made even more cats.

Theaten decided not to pursue the matter on account of not wanting to deal with a town overrun by dogs or wolves. Nicolas considered the case closed, and the people accepted that Sapari belonged to the cats.

By the time Allyra entered the galley, the old men had started their meeting. Pater Donotoris, who had fathered the first two Immolesses, and was a popular patron of the local brothel, sat bemoaning Allyra’s rampant sex drive, and her obsession with powerful beings.

Allyra had argued on several occasions that sex was a much cleaner method of extracting knowledge and exerting control than boiling and decapitation, the latter she preferred to use on local vampires to gather information about the Immortalis. The Electi did not care for this method either. Unfortunately for Allyra’s sexual suitors, those who chose to finish first generally discovered that decapitation remained very much on the table. The Electi compensated the widows just generously enough for them to forget that they had ever been married at all, and, where required, a new lord and husband would be nominated.

The Electi wore lifejackets to every meeting. They had requested black, red or white lifejackets to give a holier than thou ambience. However, the only colours available were orange and green or yellow and black plaid. These colours had been selected by one Nicolas DeSilva and made mandatory for most sea farers.

The Electi had worn lifejackets since The Great Soak of 1534 P.V. when Allyra had turned twenty-eight years old. She had been somewhat melancholy on that particular birthday as none of her circle, save for her Baers and Chester, had noticed.

In her disgruntled state, and under the influence of her beloved Chester, Allyra bored holes into the only lifeboat on the ship. She covered the bulwark in oil, and, during the next Electi meeting removed the gangplank. She waited for the whisky to take effect, then paid a local lad to yell that the ship was sinking. Allyra watched from the mast as the old men slid around the bulwark before lowering the lifeboat. The old men then, rather unceremoniously, hurled themselves overboard and attempted to clamber onto said lifeboat. Most teetered around the edge and plunged back into the sea.

The lifeboat sank and Allyra found it highly amusing to watch the old men wobble and flail about in the water. Unfortunately, two of the men could not swim and were never seen again. It was rumoured that a being in a green and orange suit intercepted their path at the estuary, held their heads under the water until they drown, then weighed their bodies down with anchors and dropped them beneath the waves, but no one could prove this.

This loss prompted a massive reshuffle within the Electi. Pater Tempus, Allyra’s father, took the seat of Ashurrel, even though he was born in Serphage, and lived on Thanata. Tempus’s Serphage seat was handed to Pater Donotoris of Lethecrown. The seat of Lethecrown was left empty, as was the seat of Doloros, and no one in the villages wanted them.

To resolve this matter, Solis appointed two rather stupid men from the island of Thanata, named them Cogitatio and Quidam, and appointed them positions way above their paygrade. Cogitatio and Quidam were just happy to escape the mines, especially since the mines had a notably growing cat population and rumours of subterranean rock monsters and fake safety officers were in circulation. This caused an issue with the canaries, who went on strike, and no one knew how to manage the increase in noxious gases and ever-growing mortality rates.

Thanata had no representation on account of the necromancer Elyas from Sihr taking tribute from the island. Elyas, everyone said, disliked interference from both the Electi and the DarkBadb, and since neither wanted an influx of Elyas’s army of the dead worrying them, they left him alone. As long as Elyas received his tributes, he was very happy minding his own business.

Pater Solis sat at the head of the table,
‘Speak your representations!’ he instructed.
‘Pater Cogitatio of Lethecrown, present.’
‘Pater Donotoris of Serphage, present.’
‘Pater Quidam of Doloros, present.’
‘Pater Opus of Khepriarth, present.’
‘Pater Susumi of Threnodyl, present.’
‘Pater Tempus of Ashurrel, present.’
‘Pater Turgidus of Togaduine, present.’
‘Pater Haren of Neferaten, present.’
‘Pater Glacies of Bratsioca, present.’
‘Pater Silva of Varjoleto, present.’
‘Pater Pomposus of Tepes, present.’
‘Pater Stultus of D’Aten, present.’
‘And Pater Solis of Sapari, present of course,’ Solis grinned, ‘Pater Opus will be taking the notes during today’s meeting.’ Solis handed a parchment and quill to one of the old men, ‘If you will Pater Opus.’

Pater Opus was quite past his sell by date, and mildly deaf, which meant he had a tendency to shout,
‘The minutes of the previous meeting are as follows; It was decided that Immoless Lucia would be sent to Corax early and that she would internally infiltrate the Immortalis, so that she could work alongside Immoless Stacia unnoticed. It has been brought to my attention by Demize the Fourth of The DarkBadb Brotherhood that Immoless Stacia is no longer with us. He received word to that effect from Lord Theaten not thirty minutes ago. Rest her soul.’
‘Rest her soul,’ the congregation replied in unison.
Everyone took a sip of drink, and as they did, Allyra sat next to her father Tempus.
‘You’re late,’ Donotoris scowled. Allyra had overheard his comments on her whoredom and chose not to respond.
Solis raised his hand,
‘Pater Opus please note that the Immoless, Allyra Cavidini D is present.’
‘WHAT?’ Opus yelled.
‘I SAID ALLYRA IS HERE!’
‘I CAN SEE THAT, I’M NOT BLIND,’ Opus shouted back.
‘WRITE IT DOWN!’

Opus set to scribbling her name anywhere on the page.
‘Now, Immoless,’ Solis began, ‘We all have faith in your sister, Lucia.’
‘She isn’t my sister,’ Allyra muttered.
‘That’s because you’re a whoring bastard,’ Donotoris growled.
Allyra jumped up and shoved her face in his,
‘Takes one to know one. I’ve seen you in the brothels…’
Tempus fidgeted awkwardly in his seat,
‘Daughter, calm yourself. Come sit.’
Allyra returned to her seat, and Tempus turned to Solis,
‘With respect Pater, Pater Donotoris’s rhetoric is reductive to our cause. He is aware that my daughter has her problems, and her turns, and must respect the role of the priestess as per The Vigilante Milkmaid Code of Conduct Section Seventeen and in accordance with Irkallan constitutional law.’

Solis thought for a while and bit his lower lip. He gurned, bit his lip again and finally made a decision,
‘There shall be no more bickering on the Solis. From anyone.’
‘She is still a whore,’ Donotoris mumbled.
Allyra stood, kicked her chair and marched past the sprawling table.
‘Where are you going?’ Solis asked.
Allyra did not even look back,
‘To the head!’
At that she exited the galley, climbed down three steep steps, and barged herself into a narrow lavatory. The head was above sea-level and had a small porthole. Allyra unscrewed the dogs and flung open the glass. She closed her eyes and breathed in the glorious sea air, then pulled her kleptobag from her back, had a quick rummage and lifted out a silver tin. Therein she located her matches and pre-rolled Ashurrel leaf joints, lit one, inhaled, held it in for maximum impact and blew the smoke out of the hole.

‘I don’t like that man!’ Nicolas said as his face drifted in front of hers. The mitre had gone, but the glasses, moustache, and his cane were quite present. Allyra leaned her head out to see what he was standing on, but there was nothing below him. She pulled her head back in and took another drag. Nicolas’s head followed hers into the head,
‘I have a suggestion, a marvellous suggestion, yes, it is. One that you shall thank me for and show eternal gratitude for as you kneel in my presence.’
Allyra took another well-earned smoke, the day was already proving to be a wearing one.
‘And what might this suggestion be, Great Lord of the Asklepion?’
Nicolas frowned,
‘It is not acceptable for you to speak to me in that way.’
‘That’s your suggestion? Noted.’

‘No Madam, that is not my suggestion,’ Nicolas said pulling his head back out of the porthole for fear that he might get stuck, or Allyra may trap him with the glass, ‘my suggestion is this; we can forego the nonsense that lies ahead, and you can marry me and I will keep you safe.’
Allyra laughed as she took another hit. Nicolas’s brows furrowed in confusion,
‘What is so amusing? I think my suggestion suits everyone.’
‘Have you actually said this to yourself out loud?’ Allyra asked.
Nicolas nodded,
‘Many times, my love.’
‘Nic,’ Allyra huffed, ‘I am not your love, and the proposition you are making is if I marry you, you will keep me safe from what? You?’
Nicolas considered Allyra’s interpretation,
‘Yes, Madam, if you marry me, I will keep you safe from me.’
Allyra glared at him, closed the porthole, screwed down the dogs, and sat baking in her own little hotbox.

Smoke filled the small room enough to mask whether Nicolas was still at the porthole or not. Allyra’s moment of peace, however, was interrupted again by Donotoris pounding on the door,
‘Whore, are you smoking in there?’
Allyra pulled out the key that hung crustily in the door and looked through the keyhole,
‘I can’t see you, Pater.’
Donotoris crouched down just as Allyra took her final drag. His eye levelled with the keyhole and Allyra exhaled a wealth of smoke straight into them. Donotoris cursed, rubbed his eyes and banged louder. Once he had finished clawing at his eyes, Donotoris muttered,
‘Bitch, your baers are here.’
Allyra waited for the old man to go back to the galley, put her paraphernalia away and popped her kleptobag back on her back.

In the galley stood two warriors draped in furs, a man, and a woman. Lycans of the baer clan. The man, BaerNedi, wore furs to match his greying beard and long hair. He carried a quiver and bow, and his belt held a sheath for a fine sword. His beloved partner, Banshee Baer had swarthy skin and long curly black hair. She wore a fur coat and fine gold jewellery to accompany a gold headband and a gold coloured skirt suit beneath. The Baers did not look at the Electi, nor speak to them. They waited, stoically for Allyra, and both smiled welcomingly as she entered the galley,
‘We have news,’ Banshee began.
Solis banged his fist on the table,
‘Excuse me, but we are in a meeting.’
Allyra smiled,
‘Opus, make a note, the third Immoless had to leave early on business.’
‘WHAT?’ Opus replied.
‘Nevermind,’ Allyra said, barging past him.
Donotoris muttered under his breath, and Tempus dropped his head into his hands as Allyra and her baers vacated the ship.

The trio marched along the quayside, and Banshee excitedly divulged much wanted information,
‘We have captured Mica, the vampire nomad from Bratsioca. We think he knows how to make that deal with Behmor.’
Allyra nodded,
‘How shall we proceed?’
‘Nedi and I will take him to The Sombre. We shall chain him, Nedi has some sturdy immortal chains, and leave him to think for a while, then you can boil him. Mica is a resilient one though, so it may take some time.’

Allyra had a few haunts in Sapari; The Sapari Tavern, the abandoned Dokeshi Carnival, and her shipwreck Sombre, a ship that had been stuck on the rocks by the DarkBadb’s headquarters, The lighthouse known as the Clachdhu Beacon, for longer than Allyra could remember. The Sombre provided an excellent site for interrogation on account of its isolation and the waves crushing any victim’s hopes of being heard. Allyra had commandeered The Sombre in 1532 P.V., a year after first meeting her baers. She had been partaking in a little too much rum with her dearest and most beloved boyfriend, Chester, and quite lost track of reality. She awoke the next day in the cabin of The Sombre with Chester.

Chester must have been feeling quite amorous since his cock had already started worrying her before her eyes opened, and she had more interest in polishing his flute than she did in how they had arrived on the shipwreck. Nonetheless, she adored the sea and was quite happy to keep the Sombre since no one else seemed to want it.

‘Perhaps,’ Allyra suggested, ‘We should leave him chained on the iron chair. A few spikes in him may help jog his memory.’
BaerNedi laughed,
‘You’re in a vicious mood today.’
Allyra stopped, raised her hands so that her palms faced the sea and said,
‘Long story. Wet wake. Stalker. Donotoris.’
With that she resumed her pace.
‘Say no more,’ Banshee replied, ‘let Nedi and I deal with Mica, and we will meet you in the tavern later. Agreed?’
Allyra nodded,
‘Agreed.’

Banshee and Nedi walked a few yards further with Allyra then stopped at a small mooring.
‘This is us then.’
Allyra looked down into the punt below. A hessian sack was chained to one of the thwarts nearest the stern. It writhed and complained but could not breach the shining chains that held it down.
‘Can you return the punt to the west quay later? I need it to get home tonight. If I spend another night in the sea my father will have a shit fit,’ Allyra asked.
‘Whatever you need, Lyra,’ Nedi said as he descended the stone steps.

Allyra continued to walk along the quayside, alone, until she reached the west wall. She climbed onto the wall and sat looking out to sea. She closed her eyes and thought of Sihr. Two warm breezes of air touched either side of her neck, as if someone was blowing on her. She opened her eyes rapidly and looked behind her, but no one was there. She turned back to the sea and by chance glanced at the pebbled beach below.

‘Arms for the poor?’ A voice called up.

Scene VII: The Detective and The Ambassador

The 2ndDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Sapari Port

‘Arms or legs for the poor,’ the voice repeated. A man wearing a hessian sack over a plaid suit sat on the beach beneath the wall. His top hat and fake moustache remained, as did his glasses. In front of his bent, gangly legs sat an open cardboard box with ‘Arms and legs for the poor,’ written on it in yellow ink, and sticking out of the box were actual, blood-soaked arms and legs, quite old ones that added a certain cadence to the sea air.

Allyra, having learned much about Nicolas from her victims, opted to ignore the grotesque art show. Instead, she jumped down from the wall and confronted Nicolas face to face,
‘Nicolas are you stalking me?’
‘I’m not Nicolas,’ the beggar replied.
‘No, you’re Pope Talking Bollocks from Corax!’
Nicolas gasped,
‘Madam, your psychic abilities astonish even me, but you may call me ‘Sir.’’
‘Sir, are you stalking me?’ Allyra reiterated, folding her arms.
Nicolas shuffled about on the harsh, thick pebbles,
‘I don’t know.’
‘You don’t know if you are stalking me?’
Nicolas’s lip moved from side to side,
‘I don’t know what stalking means.’
Allyra knelt down next to him,
‘What it means, Nic, is to follow someone when they do not want to be followed or worse to try and force someone to marry you when they are not interested. It is considered quite revolting behaviour.’

Nicolas took a few minutes to ponder over the definition. Whilst he was pondering, he rolled his eyes upwards and fixed them in a strangely precise north-east location. Dark whispers circulated about Allyra, but she put it down to one of her turns and not wanting to cause a scene, ignored it.

After a while of pondering, Nicolas rolled his eyes back into position and presented his conclusion,
‘I was here first, Madam. You came to me. I have not moved.’
Suddenly, Nicolas jumped up and started yelling, ‘CONSTABLE, CONSTABLE, CONSTABLE, A crazy lady is stalking me!’
Allyra darted back, climbed up the wall in panic and dropped onto the quayside. She looked back at the beach and Nicolas, and his box, were gone. Before she could let out a sigh of relief however, a man’s heavy hand dropped onto her shoulder, and harsh words boomed in her ear,
‘What’s going on here, then?’
Allyra turned to face the man who appeared to be Nicolas, only he was dressed in an official black suit with a long black coat and held a magnifying glass.
‘Nicolas, please stop whatever this is. It is against the rules for us to meet before we are supposed to, so…’
The man shook his head,
‘You are confused, Madam, I am Detective Cedric without a surname.’
Allyra’s face screwed up,
‘Detective what?’
‘Cedric, are you deaf?’
Her hand rubbed her forehead, and she tried to step away from his grasp, but he was too strong and would not let go.

‘I’m not deaf, no.’
‘There have been complaints about you stalking the homeless.’ Nicolai-Cedric said as he took a pencil and notebook from his inside jacket pocket, ‘Have you anything to say? Anything you do say will be used against you as you are fraternising with the nemesis and causing him a great deal of discontent.’
Allyra shook her head,
‘That’s not true. I was, well I was just going to the tavern.’
‘I see,’ Cedric replied, then scrawled some comments in his notebook whilst muttering, ‘fraternising, loitering, and an alcohol addiction.’ He then looked down at her, ‘You say you were going to the tavern, may I ask from where?’
‘The quayside.’
Detective Cedric looked up and down the quay,
‘You are on the quayside.’
‘And I am going to the tavern.’
‘But you are on the quayside, so you cannot be coming from the quayside. How did you get here?’
‘Boat.’
Detective Cedric raised an eyebrow, and started scribbling again,
‘Disorientated, possibly lying, and very confused.’
Allyra stretched the left corner of her lip to the side,
‘I’m not confused.’
‘Denies confusion does not deny the other symptoms. Symptoms confirmed, including lying.’

Cedric put his notebook back in his pocket and frowned before saying,
‘All smells very fishy to me.’ As he spoke, a handcuff clicked about Allyra’s right wrist and then its twin clicked about his left wrist, ‘I must take you to the embassy.’
‘I live here,’ Allyra argued.
