text:
🔄 100 COMPANIES THAT PIVOTED COMPLETELY FROM THEIR ORIGINAL BUSINESS

Before the brand you know, there was something very different 👇

🎮 TOYS, GAMES & ENTERTAINMENT

𝟏. 🇯🇵 Nintendo — Founded in 1889 to make hanafuda playing cards; reportedly also tried taxis, instant rice and love hotels before video games

𝟐. 🇩🇰 Lego — Carpenter Ole Kirk Christiansen made stepladders and ironing boards before wooden toys, then plastic bricks

𝟑. 🇺🇸 Hasbro — The Hassenfeld Brothers sold textile remnants, then pencil cases and school supplies, before toys

𝟒. 🇺🇸 Mattel — Started in a garage making picture frames; dollhouse furniture from the scraps led to toys

𝟓. 🇺🇸 Tonka — Mound Metalcraft made garden tools before its steel toy trucks took over

𝟔. 🇺🇸 Crayola — Binney & Smith made industrial pigments, including carbon black for tyres, before crayons (1903)

𝟕. 🇺🇸 Play-Doh — Kutol Products sold it as wallpaper cleaner before relaunching it as a toy in the 1950s

𝟖. 🇯🇵 Sega — Began as Standard Games, supplying coin-operated amusement machines to US military bases in Japan

𝟗. 🇯🇵 Konami — Started in 1969 as a jukebox rental and repair business in Osaka

𝟏𝟎. 🇯🇵 Square — Began as a software division of Den-Yu-Sha, a power-line construction company

𝟏𝟏. 🇺🇸 AOL — Grew out of GameLine, a service for downloading Atari 2600 games over phone lines

𝟏𝟐. 🇺🇸 Pixar — Sold the Pixar Image Computer, a high-end graphics machine, before making films

𝟏𝟑. 🇺🇸 Twitch — Began as https://t.co/TBH0bvr1Gu, where co-founder Justin Kan streamed his own life 24/7

𝟏𝟒. 🇺🇸 Discord — Its makers first built a mobile game, Fates Forever

𝟏𝟓. 🇺🇸 Brunswick — Billiard tables in 1845, then bowling; today mostly boats and marine engines

📱 TECH & INTERNET

𝟏𝟔. 🇫🇮 Nokia — A paper mill in 1865, then rubber boots and cables, then phones; today mostly telecom network gear

𝟏𝟕. 🇺🇸 Twitter — Born inside Odeo, a podcasting start-up squeezed out by iTunes

𝟏𝟖. 🇺🇸 YouTube — Reportedly began as a video dating site with the slogan "Tune In, Hook Up"

𝟏𝟗. 🇺🇸 Instagram — Started as Burbn, a cluttered check-in app; the founders cut it down to photos

𝟐𝟎. 🇺🇸 Slack — The internal chat tool of Tiny Speck, which was building the online game Glitch

𝟐𝟏. 🇨🇦 Flickr — A photo-sharing feature of the online game Game Neverending

𝟐𝟐. 🇨🇦 Shopify — Built to run Snowdevil, the founders' online snowboard shop

𝟐𝟑. 🇺🇸 PayPal — Confinity first offered security software and money "beaming" for PalmPilot handhelds

𝟐𝟒. 🇺🇸 Netflix — DVD rental by mail, then streaming, then a film and TV studio

𝟐𝟓. 🇺🇸 Amazon — An online bookstore in 1995; now an everything store and cloud giant (AWS)

𝟐𝟔. 🇺🇸 Groupon — Began as The Point, a platform for collective-action campaigns

𝟐𝟕. 🇺🇸 Pinterest — Grew out of Tote, a mobile shopping catalogue app

𝟐𝟖. 🇺🇸 Android — First designed as an operating system for digital cameras

𝟐𝟗. 🇺🇸 Yelp — Started as an email service for asking friends for local tips

𝟑𝟎. 🇺🇸 Fab — Began as Fabulis, a social network, before becoming a design store

𝟑𝟏. 🇺🇸 Glossier — Grew out of Into the Gloss, a beauty blog

𝟑𝟐. 🇺🇸 IBM — As CTR it made scales, time clocks, tabulators and meat slicers; later computers, now software and consulting

𝟑𝟑. 🇺🇸 Intel — A memory-chip maker that quit DRAM in the mid-1980s to bet on microprocessors

𝟑𝟒. 🇺🇸 Texas Instruments — Began as Geophysical Service Inc., doing seismic surveys for oil

𝟑𝟓. 🇺🇸 Western Digital — Made chip test equipment and calculator chips before hard drives

𝟑𝟔. 🇺🇸 Xerox — The Haloid Company made photographic paper before xerography

𝟑𝟕. 🇺🇸 Corning — Made glass bulbs for Edison's lamps; now optical fibre and smartphone cover glass

𝟑𝟖. 🇺🇸 Motorola — Galvin Manufacturing made battery eliminators for home radios, then car radios

𝟑𝟗. 🇨🇦 BlackBerry — The smartphone pioneer became a security and car-software (QNX) company

𝟒𝟎. 🇬🇧 Vodafone — Grew out of Racal Electronics, a maker of military radios

𝟒𝟏. 🇮🇳 Wipro — Western India Vegetable Products made cooking oil before IT services

𝟒𝟐. 🇯🇵 Sharp — Named after the Ever-Sharp mechanical pencil, its founder's first hit

𝟒𝟑. 🇯🇵 Brother — Began by repairing sewing machines; now best known for printers

𝟒𝟒. 🇯🇵 Fujifilm — Photographic film, then healthcare, materials and even Astalift skincare

𝟒𝟓. 🇳🇱 Philips — Light bulbs in 1891, then TVs and radios; today focused on health technology

𝟒𝟔. 🇯🇵 Sony — Reportedly its first product attempt was an electric rice cooker that flopped

🚗 CARS & MACHINES

𝟒𝟕. 🇯🇵 Toyota — Grew from Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, a maker of textile looms

𝟒𝟖. 🇯🇵 Suzuki — Made weaving looms from 1909 before motorbikes and cars

𝟒𝟗. 🇯🇵 Mazda — Started as Toyo Cork Kogyo, a cork manufacturer

𝟓𝟎. 🇯🇵 Subaru — Rooted in Nakajima Aircraft, a plane maker

𝟓𝟏. 🇯🇵 Bridgestone — Grew from the founder's family business making tabi, split-toe footwear

𝟓𝟐. 🇯🇵 Mitsubishi — Began in 1870 as a shipping company

𝟓𝟑. 🇰🇷 Kia — Made steel tubing and bicycle parts in 1944

𝟓𝟒. 🇮🇹 Lamborghini — Ferruccio Lamborghini made tractors before supercars

𝟓𝟓. 🇫🇷 Peugeot — Steel, coffee mills and pepper grinders long before cars

𝟓𝟔. 🇩🇪 BMW — Built aircraft engines before motorcycles and cars

𝟓𝟕. 🇩🇪 Porsche — Started in 1931 as an engineering design consultancy

𝟓𝟖. 🇮🇹 Ferrari — A racing team (Scuderia Ferrari, 1929) that sold its own road cars only from 1947

𝟓𝟗. 🇩🇪 Opel — Sewing machines, then bicycles, then cars

𝟔𝟎. 🇨🇿 Škoda — Its car line began with Laurin & Klement, a bicycle maker

𝟔𝟏. 🇮🇹 Ducati — Made radio components (condensers) in 1926

𝟔𝟐. 🇮🇹 Piaggio — Ship fittings and aircraft before the Vespa scooter (1946)

𝟔𝟑. 🇸🇪 Volvo — Started as a unit of ball-bearing maker SKF; "Volvo" is Latin for "I roll"

𝟔𝟒. 🇸🇪 Husqvarna — A musket factory founded in 1689; now chainsaws and lawn mowers

𝟔𝟓. 🇯🇵 Yamaha — An organ and piano maker whose machining skills led to Yamaha motorcycles (1955)

𝟔𝟔. 🇨🇳 BYD — Rechargeable phone batteries, then electric cars

👜 FASHION & BEAUTY

𝟔𝟕. 🇺🇸 Tiffany & Co. — Opened in 1837 as a stationery and "fancy goods" store

𝟔𝟖. 🇫🇷 Hermès — Harnesses and saddles for horses (1837)

𝟔𝟗. 🇫🇷 Chanel — Began as a hat shop (1910)

𝟕𝟎. 🇺🇸 Levi's — A dry-goods wholesaler for 20 years before jeans (1873)

𝟕𝟏. 🇺🇸 Nike — As Blue Ribbon Sports it imported Onitsuka Tiger shoes from Japan

𝟕𝟐. 🇺🇸 Abercrombie & Fitch — An elite outfitter of guns, tents and fishing gear before teen fashion

𝟕𝟑. 🇺🇸 Avon — A door-to-door book seller gave away perfume samples; the perfume won

𝟕𝟒. 🇯🇵 Shiseido — A Western-style pharmacy in Tokyo (1872)

𝟕𝟓. 🇰🇷 LG — Lak-Hui Chemical made "Lucky" face cream

𝟕𝟔. 🇺🇸 Colgate — Starch, soap and candles (1806)

𝟕𝟕. 🇺🇸 Kleenex — Cellucotton, a WWI bandage material, relaunched as cold-cream remover tissue

𝟕𝟖. 🇺🇸 Listerine — A surgical antiseptic, also marketed as a floor cleaner

🍫 FOOD & DRINK

𝟕𝟗. 🇺🇸 Wrigley — Sold soap, then baking powder; the free chewing gum became the product

𝟖𝟎. 🇺🇸 Hershey — The Lancaster Caramel Company, sold in 1900 to focus on chocolate

𝟖𝟏. 🇺🇸 Coca-Cola — Sold in pharmacies as a patent "brain tonic"

𝟖𝟐. 🇺🇸 Pepsi — "Brad's Drink", sold as a digestive aid

𝟖𝟑. 🇺🇸 Kellogg's — Corn flakes were made as health food for sanitarium patients

𝟖𝟒. 🇺🇸 Starbucks — Sold only beans and coffee gear; espresso drinks came later

𝟖𝟓. 🇺🇸 Marriott — An A&W root beer stand in Washington, D.C. (1927)

𝟖𝟔. 🇺🇸 McDonald's — A barbecue drive-in (1940) before burgers

𝟖𝟕. 🇰🇷 Samsung — A 1938 trading firm selling dried fish, vegetables and noodles

𝟖𝟖. 🇮🇳 Reliance — Polyester yarn trading, then oil refining and telecom

🏭 INDUSTRY, ENERGY & MONEY

𝟖𝟗. 🇬🇧 Shell — Marcus Samuel's family sold seashells before oil

𝟗𝟎. 🇸🇪 IKEA — Pens, wallets, picture frames and nylon stockings by mail

𝟗𝟏. 🇺🇸 3M — A mine that turned out worthless, then sandpaper, tape and Post-it Notes

𝟗𝟐. 🇺🇸 DuPont — Gunpowder mills (1802), then chemicals and nylon

𝟗𝟑. 🇺🇸 Berkshire Hathaway — A struggling textile mill turned into Warren Buffett's conglomerate

𝟗𝟒. 🇺🇸 American Express — Express freight and parcel delivery (1850)

𝟗𝟓. 🇺🇸 Western Union — The telegraph giant became a money-transfer company

𝟗𝟔. 🇬🇧 Virgin — A student magazine, then mail-order records; later airlines and trains

𝟗𝟕. 🇩🇰 Ørsted — Oil and gas (DONG Energy) to offshore wind power

𝟗𝟖. 🇸🇪🇫🇮 Stora Enso — A copper mine at Falun, Sweden, now paper and wood products

𝟗𝟗. 🇫🇮 Wärtsilä — A sawmill in 1834; now marine engines and power plants

text:
After a wedding watched by the world, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce slipped away to Montana, choosing mountain privacy over a honeymoon filled with cameras, crowds, and carefully staged appearances.

According to the story, they married on July 3, 2026, at Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Around 1,000 guests attended the celebration.

But afterward, the couple wanted something entirely different.

Silence.

Privacy.

And a few days together.

Their destination was the Yellowstone Club in Big Sky, Montana.

Far from the crowds that had followed their romance.

Their relationship began attracting attention in 2023.

Travis spoke publicly about Taylor.

Soon afterward, she appeared at a Kansas City Chiefs game beside his mother, Donna.

What began with a friendship-bracelet story eventually led to their August 2025 engagement.

Then came the wedding.

Pat McAfee, who attended with his wife, described the celebration as an extraordinary gathering of football, Hollywood, and Nashville.

But the newlyweds' private retreat offered something no enormous party could.

Time without an audience.

Their larger honeymoon plans reportedly included several remarkable destinations.

The Bahamas.

Lake Como.

Paris and the French Riviera.

Croatia, Greece, Singapore, and Australia.

Each promised a different experience.

Caribbean sunshine, European coastlines, peaceful islands, and distant cities.

Croatia also carried a connection to Kelce's family roots.

Yet the appeal wasn't simply luxury.

For two people whose lives unfold under constant public attention, uninterrupted time together had become precious.

Someone familiar with the plans reportedly said they intended to remain off the grid.

Friends and family had been informed.

The couple wanted space to enjoy their marriage privately.

But professional responsibilities complicated the schedule.

Kelce's return to football training reportedly delayed their longer journey.

For now, Montana remained their first newlywed escape.

A place where the enormous wedding celebration could become a memory rather than another public event.

The rest of their travels could wait.

Their marriage had begun with thousands watching.

Their next chapter was meant for just two people.

And perhaps the greatest luxury wasn't another beautiful destination.

It was finally having a moment that belonged only to them.

✨ The Devutthana Ekadashi Puja Vidhi centers on symbolically awakening Lord Sri Vishnu from his four-month Yoga Nidra during Pradosh Kaal (sunset) or evening worship, followed by bhakti chanting and lamps.

Step-by-Step Devutthana Ekadashi Puja Vidhi:-
Purification & Altar Setup:Clean the puja area, take a bath, and wear clean yellow, white, or light-colored clothes. Spread a yellow cloth on a wooden platform (chowki) and place idols or images of Lord Sri Vishnu (or Shaligram) and Goddess Lakshmi Maa.
Sankalpa (Sacred Vow):Light a ghee lamp (diya) and incense. Hold water, a flower, and sesame seeds (til—avoid rice on Ekadashi) in your right hand and take a vow to observe the fast and puja with devotion.
Abhishekam & Adornment:Bathe the Sri Vishnu/Shaligram Idol with clean water and Panchamrit (milk, curd, ghee, honey, and sugar), followed by pure water. Wipe gently, dress the Deity in yellow attire, and apply chandan (sandalwood) and haldi tilak.
Symbolic Awakening (Dev Uthan):Traditionally, devotees draw footprints of Lord Sri Vishnu leading toward the puja room or courtyard using geru (red ochre) and white paste/flour. Gently ring a bell, blow a conch (shankha), or tap a brass plate while chanting awakening prayers to invite the Lord to rise.
Offerings (Naivedya):Offer yellow flowers, marigold garlands, sugarcane stalks, singhara (water chestnuts), ber, sweet potatoes, seasonal fruits, and sattvic sweets. Always include Tulsi leaves in Lord Sri Vishnu’s bhog (never pluck Tulsi leaves on Ekadashi itself; use leaves plucked the previous day or naturally fallen ones).
Katha, Jaap & Aarti:Read or listen to the Devutthana Ekadashi Vrat Katha, chant Sri Vishnu mantras or the Sri Vishnu Sahasranama, and conclude with Om Jai Jagdish Hare Aarti. Light extra ghee diyas near the altar and the Tulsi plant in the evening.

Recommended Mantras:
1. Lord Vishnu Awakening Mantra (Prabodhan Mantra)
Chant while ringing the bell to symbolically awaken Lord Vishnu:
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ गोविन्द उत्तिष्ठ गरुडध्वज ।
उत्तिष्ठ कमलाकान्त त्रैलोक्यं मङ्गलं कुरु ॥
Uttishthottishtha Govinda uttishtha Garudadhwaja |
Uttishtha Kamalakanta trailokyam mangalam kuru ||
Meaning: "Arise, O Govinda, arise, O Garuda-bannered Lord; arise, O Beloved of Kamala (Lakshmi), and bring auspiciousness to the three worlds."

2. Dwadashakshari Mantra (For Japa & Meditation)
ॐ नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय ॥
Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya ||

3. Vishnu Gayatri Mantra
ॐ नारायणाय विद्महे वासुदेवाय धीमहि । तन्नो विष्णुः प्रचोदयात् ॥
Om Narayanaya Vidmahe Vasudevaya Dhimahi | Tanno Vishnuh Prachodayat ||

4. Tulsi Pranama Mantra (While Offering Water/Lamps to Tulsi)
वृन्दायाई तुलसीदेव्यै प्रियायै केशवस्य च ।
विष्णुभक्तिप्रदे देवि सत्यवत्यै नमो नमः ॥
Vrindayai Tulsidevyai Priyayai Keshavasya Cha |
Vishnubhaktiprade Devi Satyavatyai Namo Namah ||

Arsenal may be building a team capable of winning major trophies, but could their style of football prevent Rice from reaching individual greatness?

text:
⛪️ Little Church Down the Way
Many Waters Cannot Quench Love
Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.
Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
Song of Solomon 8:6–7 KJV
There’s a moment just before our passage that I’d like us to see. Someone asks who is coming up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved. Then the woman speaks. She is already close enough to lean on him, yet there is something she still wants to ask. Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm.
There is courage in asking for that much. A lovely afternoon can tell you that someone enjoys your company. It takes longer to learn what place you have in their life. She asks him plainly.
Upon thine heart, upon thine arm
A seal in the ancient Near East could identify the person to whom it belonged. Pressed into clay, it left a distinctive mark, much as a signature identifies the person who made it. That gives the woman’s image some of its force. She asks her beloved to carry the mark of their love on his heart and on his arm. 
I hear two things in that request. The heart is the place of inward affection, where another person can be dear to you in a way the world may never see. The arm suggests the strength with which you act. Put the two together, and you can hear what she is asking. Let me be dear to you in your heart, and let me see it in the life you live.
A person learns what place they have with us in a hundred ordinary ways. They learn it when we remember what they told us yesterday. They learn it when we keep a promise that has become inconvenient. They learn it when there is a hard thing to say and we care enough to say it truthfully and kindly. The arm gives the heart away.
Love is strong as death
That is a startling thing to say in a love poem. The woman takes something both of them know to be relentless and uses it to speak of love’s strength. Then the images grow more severe. There is the grave, and then there is fire. Her words give love all the seriousness it deserves.
The word jealousy gives the woman’s longing for faithfulness a fierce edge. She speaks that longing openly to her beloved. The faithfulness she asks for is something each person must give freely and live out with care.
Then come the waters. Listen to how the verse builds. First there are many waters. Then there are floods. I think of people who have stood beside each other through a year they would scarcely know how to describe. They have taken turns being the one who could get up and do what needed doing. They have found ways to be gentle with each other while they were both worn thin. They may smile a little when they hear the verse read. They know how high the water can rise. They know something about the flame as well.
All the substance of his house
At the end of the passage, the woman imagines a man offering everything he owns for love. The offer would be utterly contemned. In plain words, it would be despised.
I’m glad the Song puts that image last. After the fire and the flood, along comes a man with everything he owns, thinking he can settle the matter by naming a price. He can spend all he has and still have no claim on another person’s heart. Think how much kindness there is in that truth. A person with very little to give can love faithfully for a lifetime. Some of us learned that from people whose gifts were as plain as a ride home, a place at the table, or an evening they could have spent any other way.
The love of God in Christ
The Song has taught us to listen closely to two people who love each other. It also gives us words to carry with us when we turn to the New Testament and hear Paul speak of the love of God in Christ.
 For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
 Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Romans 8:38–39 KJV
Paul puts death on his list, and he puts tomorrow there too. Things to come. Perhaps that is the phrase somebody in our little church needs this morning. You may have come in carrying a fear about what will happen when you go home, or what next week will bring. You can leave with this assurance from Scripture. Whatever tomorrow brings, it cannot separate you from the love of God in Christ Jesus.
And as we go, there may be somebody who needs to see in our arm what we’ve been keeping in our heart. We could make the visit. Keep the promise. Say what we have meant to say for years. There’s a good chance they already know we love them. It will still do them good to see it.
Lord, thank You for the love You have given us in Christ. Teach us to love faithfully in the ordinary things we do, and give us the courage to let the people we love see it. Amen.

English

Nov. 19 U.S. close: S&P 500 −2.02%, Nasdaq Composite −2.25%, Dow −2.19%. Three signals worth watching across Asia:

1. Market breadth matters more than a few resilient giants.
Over 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell. That points to broad risk aversion. For China, Japan and Korea, a steady headline index alone would be weak evidence of recovery. Watch how many stocks participate, and whether strength spreads beyond heavyweight names.

2. Chip stocks can reprice before orders change.
Nvidia fell 3.30%; AMD lost 7.72%. My read: Japanese chip equipment, Korean memory and China’s computing supply chain face pressure on the valuations investors will pay. Share-price weakness alone doesn’t establish canceled orders. Earnings guidance and actual orders remain the stronger test.

3. Lower Treasury yields may offer less relief than expected.
The U.S. 10-year yield eased from 5.07% to 5.04%, while the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index fell from 20.9 to 6.3, still positive. Cheaper discount rates can help valuations, but softer demand can hurt earnings. For Asian exporters, the order book deserves as much attention as the bond market.

中文

美东11月19日收盘：标普500跌2.02%，纳指跌2.25%，道指跌2.19%。对亚洲市场，值得盯住三个传导点：

1、指数抗跌，还要看多少股票跟得上。
标普500超过九成成分股下跌，说明风险偏好收缩的范围很广。观察A股、日经和韩综，不能只看几只权重股能否撑住指数，还要看上涨家数，以及强势能否从大盘股扩散出去。

2、芯片股估值可以先跌，订单未必同步变差。
英伟达跌3.30%，AMD跌7.72%。我的判断：日本半导体设备、韩国存储，以及A股算力产业链，可能先承受估值压力。股价下跌本身不能证明客户取消订单；真正需要核对的是业绩指引和实际订单。

3、美债收益率回落，未必足以托住出口链。
美国10年期国债收益率从5.07%降至5.04%；费城联储制造业指数从20.9降至6.3，仍为正值。利率下降有助估值，但需求放缓可能压低盈利。看亚洲出口企业，订单簿和美债曲线同样重要。

日本語

米国11月19日終値：S&P500は2.02％安、ナスダック総合は2.25％安、ダウは2.19％安。アジア株への波及で見るべき点は3つ。

1、指数の底堅さと、相場全体の底堅さを分けて見る。
S&P500構成銘柄の9割超が下落。リスク回避が広い範囲に及んだ。中国A株、日経平均、KOSPIも、大型株だけで指数を支えているなら回復の判断は慎重に。値上がり銘柄数と、買いの広がりを確認したい。

2、半導体株の評価は、受注より先に変わる。
エヌビディアは3.30％安、AMDは7.72％安。日本の半導体製造装置、韓国のメモリー、中国のAIインフラ関連には、まずバリュエーション面の圧力が波及しうる。ただし、株安だけで受注取り消しは確認できない。業績見通しと実際の受注が判断材料になる。

3、米金利の低下だけでは、輸出株を支えきれない可能性。
米10年債利回りは5.07％から5.04％へ低下。一方、フィラデルフィア連銀製造業指数は20.9から6.3へ低下し、プラス圏を維持した。割引率の低下は株価評価を支えても、需要減速は利益を圧迫しうる。輸出企業では金利と同じくらい受注動向を見たい。

한국어

미국 현지 11월 19일 마감: S&P500 −2.02%, 나스닥종합 −2.25%, 다우 −2.19%. 아시아 증시로 이어질 세 가지 경로를 살펴본다.

1、지수보다 상승 종목의 폭을 확인할 때.
S&P500 구성 종목의 90% 이상이 하락했다. 위험회피가 시장 전반으로 확산됐다는 신호다. 중국 A주·닛케이·코스피에서도 일부 대형주가 지수를 지탱하는 것만으로 회복을 판단하기는 어렵다. 상승 종목 수와 매수세의 확산이 중요하다.

2、반도체 주가의 재평가는 주문 변화보다 빠를 수 있다.
엔비디아는 3.30%, AMD는 7.72% 하락했다. 일본 반도체 장비, 한국 메모리, 중국 AI 인프라 관련주는 우선 밸류에이션 압력을 받을 수 있다. 다만 주가 하락만으로 주문 취소를 단정할 수는 없다. 실적 가이던스와 실제 수주를 확인해야 한다.

3、미 국채금리 하락의 효과를 수요 둔화가 상쇄할 수 있다.
미국 10년물 금리는 5.07%에서 5.04%로 내려갔다. 필라델피아 연은 제조업지수는 20.9에서 6.3으로 낮아졌지만 플러스는 유지했다. 할인율 하락은 주가 평가에 도움이 돼도, 수요 둔화는 이익을 압박할 수 있다. 아시아 수출기업은 금리만큼 주문 흐름도 중요하다.

Tiếng Việt

Phiên Mỹ ngày 19/11: S&P 500 giảm 2,02%, Nasdaq Composite giảm 2,25%, Dow giảm 2,19%. Ba điểm cần theo dõi khi tác động lan sang châu Á:

1、Độ rộng thị trường quan trọng hơn vài cổ phiếu trụ.
Hơn 90% cổ phiếu trong S&P 500 giảm giá, cho thấy tâm lý né rủi ro lan rộng. Với cổ phiếu A Trung Quốc, Nikkei và KOSPI, chỉ số được vài mã lớn giữ nhịp chưa đủ chứng minh thị trường hồi phục. Cần xem số mã tăng và sức mua có lan tỏa hay không.

2、Định giá cổ phiếu chip có thể giảm trước khi đơn hàng thay đổi.
Nvidia giảm 3,30%, AMD giảm 7,72%. Theo tôi, thiết bị bán dẫn Nhật Bản, bộ nhớ Hàn Quốc và chuỗi hạ tầng AI Trung Quốc có thể chịu áp lực định giá trước. Giá cổ phiếu giảm chưa chứng minh khách hàng hủy đơn. Triển vọng lợi nhuận và đơn hàng thực tế mới là phép kiểm chứng.

3、Lợi suất Mỹ giảm chưa chắc đủ nâng đỡ nhóm xuất khẩu.
Lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ kỳ hạn 10 năm giảm từ 5,07% xuống 5,04%. Chỉ số sản xuất của Fed Philadelphia giảm từ 20,9 xuống 6,3 nhưng vẫn dương. text:
🗞️20 November 2026 | Daily Edition: Pre-Market

IBIT Logged Its Worst Day, BTC Found Buyers at $61,220

BTC set a fresh 4-month low at $61,220 in the evening and climbed back to $62,000 on higher lows through Asia, while IBIT posted a record $541 million outflow, Tether burned 4 billion USDT, the Binance thief shifted $345 million more Ether and a wrapped Monero token lost 99%.

Prepared around 5:55 AM EST on Friday 20 November. This edition picks up from Thursday's US Close, prepared at 3:50 PM EST, and only adds what happened since: the evening session, Strategy's investor Q&A, Thursday's fund flows, Asia and the first hours of Europe. Crypto prices are live prints as of about 5:50 AM EST, and futures, oil, Treasury, dollar and gold figures are live overnight prints.

1⃣ Bitcoin printed $61,220 after dark, then built four higher lows

Bitcoin was near $62,075 to $62,100 at last night's edition. It slid after the close to $61,350 at 4:30 PM EST, bounced to $62,285 at 5:45 PM EST while Strategy's Q&A was running, and spiked to an evening high of $62,562 at 8:05 PM EST. That move failed fast. Between 8:35 and 8:50 PM EST, during the Asian morning as Korean and Japanese chip stocks sold off, Bitcoin dropped about $1,000 to $61,225, about $1,300 below the 8:05 PM EST high, and it printed the session low of $61,220 at 9:10 PM EST, its lowest trade since early July. From there each dip stopped higher than the last: $61,314 at 11:35 PM EST, $61,358 just after midnight, $61,402 at 2:30 AM EST and $61,485 at 4:40 AM EST. Rallies were capped at $62,330 at 10:00 PM EST and then at about $62,000 three times in the Asia session, at 1:45 AM, 2:00 AM and 3:30 AM EST, until a push at 5:30 AM EST broke through to $62,281. It trades near $62,000, roughly flat against last night's edition and about 2.8% lower over 24 hours. Thursday's UTC daily candle closed at about $61,913, just under the $62,000 pivot.

🖊️ Market significance: Sellers extended Thursday's breakdown by only about $440 below the $61,658 afternoon low and never tested $61,000. Four higher lows after 9:10 PM EST gave the night the shape of a base, but the daily close still sits below the old floor.

🗨️ My viewpoint: I read the night as a failed follow-through, not a reversal. Sellers had a clean break and could only stretch it about 0.7%. One push to $62,281 does not reclaim anything, though. I need a daily close above $62,000, then a trade through $62,562, before I stop treating rallies as selling opportunities.

2⃣ Ether undercut its mid-November low for an hour, Zcash slid about 12%

Ether was near $1,760 to $1,762 at last night's edition. It reached $1,768 at 8:05 PM EST, fell with Bitcoin to $1,721 at 8:50 PM EST and kept going to $1,715.85 at 11:35 PM EST, under Wednesday's $1,731 low and the $1,728 low from 14 November, its weakest print since 15 November. It held $1,718 just after midnight and then climbed on higher lows at about $1,736, $1,737 and $1,741 to $1,761 at 5:35 AM EST. It trades near $1,755, about 0.3% below last night's edition and about 2.7% lower over 24 hours. Solana is near $72.40, down about 2.8% on the day after a $71.51 low at 9:00 PM EST. XRP is near $0.963, down about 2%, after a $0.9467 low in the same hour. Zcash is the weak spot again, near $836 to $844 and down about 11% to 12%, and HYPE is near $65, down about 4% to 5%.

🖊️ Market significance: The $1,748 double low that held through Thursday's US session gave way in the evening, so Ether's relative strength did not survive Asia. Its recovery since has the same higher-low shape as Bitcoin's.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Ether undercut the 14 November low and was bought back within hours. I count that as a successful retest only if $1,741 holds into the US open. Zcash losing about 12% in one session tells me the speculative corners of the market are still being sold hardest.

3⃣ Over $600 million in leverage was flushed, and offshore funding turned negative

More than $600 million of crypto futures were liquidated over 24 hours, the large majority of it longs, with close to half of it landing in the twelve hours to late Thursday evening. Since the US Close, Bitcoin perpetual open interest on the largest on-chain perps venue slipped about 1.2% to about 39,720 BTC, while on a large offshore exchange it rose about 2.7% to about 33,990 BTC. Funding on the offshore venue flipped from about plus 0.006% to about minus 0.003% per eight hours, and on the on-chain venue it eased from about minus 0.006% to about minus 0.002%. Ether open interest was flat on-chain at about 610,900 ETH and fell about 1.8% offshore to about 667,900 ETH.

🖊️ Market significance: The evening drop was a long liquidation event. The bounce since came while offshore traders added Bitcoin shorts and paid to hold them.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Negative funding with rising offshore open interest at a four-month low is the kind of crowding that feeds squeezes, and the 5:30 AM EST push to $62,281 may be the first sign of it. I want open interest to fall on further gains, which would confirm shorts covering, before I trust the bounce.

4⃣ IBIT posted the largest daily outflow in its history

US spot Bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of about $582 million on Thursday, the third outflow day in a row and the largest of the three. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for about $541 million of it, its biggest one-day withdrawal since launching in January 2024, above the roughly $528 million record from 30 January this year, and about 93% of the day's total. Fidelity's FBTC lost about $46 million, ARK's ARKB about $31 million and Grayscale's GBTC about $14 million. The one meaningful inflow was Morgan Stanley's MSBT at about $50 million. That takes November's net Bitcoin ETF outflows to about $3.47 billion. Spot Ether ETFs lost about $131 million, their fourth straight outflow day, with about $124 million leaving BlackRock's ETHA. The Solana funds lost about $1 million, all from Grayscale's GSOL.

🖊️ Market significance: The selling was concentrated in one fund, while a product sold through a wirehouse network took money in on the same day.

🗨️ My viewpoint: A record IBIT redemption on the day Bitcoin broke its weekly floor looks like a few large holders de-risking into the stock selloff, not a broad investor exit. ETHA's $124 million is the bigger surprise to me, since Ether had held up better on price. I still want two or three IBIT inflow days in a row before I call the flows turned.

5⃣ Third-quarter filings showed institutions bought about $4.1 billion of Bitcoin funds before the slide

An analysis of third-quarter 13F filings published overnight showed institutions bought a net 49,229 BTC worth of US spot Bitcoin fund shares between July and September, about $4.11 billion at 30 September prices. That was the largest quarterly purchase since the second quarter of 2025 and more than offset the 47,054 BTC they had sold, net, over the previous nine months. Wealth platforms did half the buying and now hold a record 40.5% of institutionally reported shares, led by Wells Fargo, whose holdings rose by 14,636 BTC to 30,553 BTC, the largest position of any filer. Brevan Howard added 8,606 BTC and Millennium 7,114 BTC, though the filings exclude short positions, so hedge fund buying may be part of basis trades. The 50 largest holders added 59,578 BTC while everyone else sold a net 10,349 BTC. By 16 November, the funds held 38,531 fewer BTC than at the end of September.

🖊️ Market significance: The advisor channel, the stickiest money in these funds, was growing fastest just before the drawdown began.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is a backward-looking print, and the ETF flows since September have already reversed most of it. What I take from it is who gets tested next. Advisors who run target allocations should be rebalancing buyers at these prices, and February's filings will show whether they were.

6⃣ Tether burned 4 billion USDT, and Bitfinex sent another $413 million back to the issuer

At about 8:03 PM EST, Tether burned 4 billion USDT at its treasury address on Ethereum. The tokens came from Tether's own inventory, which sits outside public circulation, so the burn does not by itself mean a fresh $4 billion drop in circulating USDT. Within minutes, about 230 million and 183 million USDT moved from Bitfinex back to the Tether treasury. Circulating USDT is about $175 billion, and USDC is about $68.5 billion to $68.7 billion.

🖊️ Market significance: The burn is housekeeping on supply that was never issued, but the Bitfinex transfers are flows back to the issuer, which usually come before redemptions.

🗨️ My viewpoint: I do not read the 4 billion burn as $4 billion leaving crypto. I do read the steady return of USDT from exchanges to the issuer as dry powder shrinking, and that lines up with what the ETF flows are saying.

7⃣ A founder-linked wallet owes half of Sky's fully borrowed pool, and the council added buybacks

After Thursday's $1.5 billion exit from Sky's USDC reserve, USDS circulating supply ended the day down about 39%, roughly 2 billion fewer tokens, with one Ethereum swap alone burning 400 million USDS for USDC. Overnight the focus moved to Sky's stUSDS lending pool, which is fully borrowed and in which a wallet tied to founder Rune Christensen owes about half the debt. Liquidations for that collateral type are switched off, and the 2.5-cent SKY price cap that governs those loans was proposed by Christensen in a forum post last year. Separately, the Sky council set out a seven-day plan that adds 750,000 USDS of daily SKY buybacks, designed to keep the daily USDS allocation for staking rewards roughly steady. USDS is still at its $1 peg.

🖊️ Market significance: The governance question has moved from who withdrew to who borrows. A founder-linked position in a pool with liquidations disabled is a credit risk that other depositors cannot hedge.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The peg holding is the good news. The concentration story keeps getting worse: one holder drained the reserve, and one wallet carries half the debt of the protocol's highest-yielding pool. Buybacks support the token, not the balance sheet, and I want the reserve's USDC buffer rebuilt before I treat Sky as stable again.

8⃣ Saylor put STRC holders first and named a $5 billion floor for the preferred

At Thursday evening's investor Q&A, Michael Saylor said he sees "natural, organic" demand for STRC at its 12% dividend somewhere between $5 billion and $7.5 billion, and that Strategy is willing to let the preferred shrink toward $5 billion through buybacks rather than raise the rate to 15% or 20%. Chief executive Phong Le said the company has bought back about $3 billion of STRC at prices between $95 and $99. Saylor said that "when the company is swapping either BTC or MSTR for STRC, we're supporting the credit," described a credit-market contraction that began around May and said Strategy has at least three years of dollar coverage. Strategy held 850,849 BTC as of 15 November. MSTR closed Thursday down about 4.6% at $86.13 and is near $86 before the bell. Among miners, PowerCompute's quarterly filing showed it had its lender sell about 267 pledged BTC in September to repay nearly $22 million of debt, and it ended the month with about $650,000 in cash and a going-concern warning.

🖊️ Market significance: The largest corporate holder has now said openly that Bitcoin is one of the tools it could use to support its preferred stock.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is the most important change in tone from Strategy this cycle. It is a statement of capacity, not a sale, but the market will now price the possibility. The level I care about is STRC's distance from $100: the further below par it trades, the closer that option gets.

9⃣ The Binance thief shifted 197,460 more ETH, and the freeze order names Circle

Between about 3:10 and 3:40 AM EST, the wallet holding funds from the 29 October theft from Binance's hot wallets moved 197,460 ETH, about $345 million, in 17 transactions. The receiving address split it into 16 batches of about 12,000 ETH each and one of about 5,460 ETH. That follows the $248 million of Ether the thief moved earlier this week. Separately, the Abu Dhabi court order that Binance disclosed on 18 November requires Circle and World Liberty Financial, among 18 named firms, to keep tokens tied to the theft frozen and not lend, swap or mix them, ahead of a 1 December hearing on whether to extend the injunction.

🖊️ Market significance: Splitting about $345 million of Ether into fresh addresses is a laundering step, and it lands on a thin, falling market.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The supply risk is real if this Ether reaches exchanges or swap venues, so I am watching those 16 addresses. The order matters for the whole industry, because it shows stablecoin issuers that a court, not just their own policy, can lock assets in place.

1⃣0⃣ A wrapped Monero token lost 99% after a wallet funded from its creator address sold

XMR1, a wrapped Monero token issued by the Wagyu swap service and traded against USDC on the order book of the largest on-chain perps venue, collapsed more than 99% early Friday. A wallet that received 5.2 million XMR1 in three transfers from the token's creator address sold into the book, taking the price from nearly $488 to $1 in about 30 minutes, and it was later trading near 91 cents. The proceeds, about $13.2 million of USDC, were swapped for 7,467 ETH. It is not yet clear whether the transfers were authorized or involved compromised keys. Monero itself and the venue's XMR perpetual were not affected, with the perpetual near $480.

🖊️ Market significance: A wrapped asset carries its issuer's key risk on top of the asset's own, and this one went to almost zero in half an hour while the underlying coin barely moved.

🗨️ My viewpoint: This is bridge risk in its purest form. Anyone holding a wrapped token on an order book is trusting whoever controls the mint, and I would apply that lesson well beyond Monero.

1⃣1⃣ Coinbase plans its own prediction markets, and the Senate voted to ban death bets

Coinbase is planning in-house US prediction markets for retail and institutional customers, targeting the first half of 2027, according to a report late Thursday. The event contracts it offers today are run by Kalshi. Coinbase also filed comments backing the CFTC's proposals to explicitly include event contracts in the definition of a swap and to exclude casino-style gambling products. The Senate passed the Death Bets Act, a bipartisan bill that would bar CFTC-registered venues from listing contracts tied to death, terrorism, assassination and war, and it now goes to the House. And a split federal appeals panel upheld the denial of Kalshi's request for a preliminary injunction against Maryland's sports-betting enforcement.

🖊️ Market significance: The largest US crypto exchange wants to own the product rather than rent it, just as Congress and the courts start drawing the edges of what can be listed.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Coinbase building its own markets is a threat to Kalshi's distribution, not to the category. The Death Bets Act is narrow and the industry can live with it. The Maryland loss is the bigger risk, because state-by-state fights are what keep sports contracts in limbo.

1⃣2⃣ VanEck dropped Gemini as a custodian for its Bitcoin, Ether and Solana ETFs

VanEck gave Gemini Trust notice ending its custody and clearing agreements for the VanEck Bitcoin ETF (HODL), Ethereum ETF (ETHV) and Solana ETF (VSOL), effective on or about 16 February 2027, according to 8-K filings signed on 19 November. Coinbase Custody will stay on as custodian for all three. Gemini has held part of each fund's crypto and cash since launch and settled the funds' crypto trades. The filings give no reason and do not say whether the assets held with Gemini will move to Coinbase.

🖊️ Market significance: ETF custody, already concentrated, is becoming more concentrated in a single provider.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Nothing changes for holders before February. For the industry, losing this mandate hurts Gemini's institutional business, and the single-custodian risk in US crypto ETFs keeps growing. That is a question regulators will eventually ask.

1⃣3⃣ Securitize reached a record $5 billion in tokenized assets, and Anthropic kept trading on-chain

Securitize reported third-quarter revenue of $18.6 million, up 13% from a year earlier and 29% from the second quarter, with tokenization revenue up 28% to $11.5 million and average tokenized assets at a record $5.0 billion, up 39%. It posted a net loss of $66.3 million. Standard Chartered extended its tokenized deposit transfers to Singapore, so eligible clients can move bank balances between Singapore and Hong Kong in near real time on the bank's own ledger, in currencies including US dollars, euros and offshore yuan. Anthropic traded through the night on-chain: its Nasdaq pre-market price is about $91.24, down about 6% from Thursday's $97.17 close, and the on-chain perpetual on the largest perps venue is near $91.27, while Coinbase's ANTc, a share-backed certificate rather than direct stock ownership, began trading on Base.

🖊️ Market significance: Tokenization revenue is growing while the business still loses money, and the on-chain Anthropic price is tracking the regulated pre-market to within a few cents.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Record tokenized assets at Securitize and bank-run deposit tokens at Standard Chartered are the plumbing story I care about more than any price this week. The Anthropic perpetual matching the pre-market is now routine, and that is exactly the point.

1⃣4⃣ Rupee withdrawals slowed at three exchanges, and the UK lobby pushed back on DeFi rules

Rupee withdrawals ran into problems at three crypto exchanges serving India: Coinbase is routing new requests through support, CoinDCX reports slower transfers and ZebPay has reported bank-related delays. In the UK, the trade body CryptoUK, which says it represents more than 150 firms, told the FCA that software development, maintenance, security work and taking part in decentralised governance should not, by themselves, make someone a regulated person under the new crypto regime. In the US, the SEC charged eight Colorado-based entities with taking more than $37 million from investors by posing as SEC-licensed crypto platforms.

🖊️ Market significance: Fiat rails are the weak link in India right now, and the UK is still deciding whether DeFi developers count as intermediaries.

🗨️ My viewpoint: The Indian delays matter most to me because they hit three venues at once, which points to the banking side rather than one exchange. If they run into next week, local premiums and stablecoin demand will show how much money is stuck.

1⃣5⃣ Bitcoin developers put a post-quantum signature on the table, and Solana resumed upgrades

Blockstream researchers Jonas Nick and Mikhail Kudinov published a draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal and security analysis for SHRINCS, a hash-based signature scheme anchored in SHA-256, which Bitcoin already uses. It pairs a compact stateful signature with a larger stateless fallback, and the compact path can let an attacker forge a signature if a one-time state is accidentally reused. Solana developers resumed network upgrades with a warning that direct mapping, still pending on mainnet with no firm activation date, brings memory rules that can break unsafe account access and some older Anchor programs.

🖊️ Market significance: Bitcoin's quantum debate is moving from whether to how, and Solana's upgrade pipeline is moving again after a pause.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Building on SHA-256 is the conservative path, and I expect it to win support for that reason. The trade-off is wallet safety: a scheme that fails if a wallet reuses state needs very good wallet software before it is anywhere near activation.

1⃣6⃣ Asia's chip rout pressed Nasdaq futures again

Japan's Nikkei 225 closed down about 5.1% at 56,437 and South Korea's Kospi down about 5.2% at 4,870, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix down about 6% to 7%, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell about 2%. European stocks are lower. Nasdaq 100 futures are down about 1% to 1.4% and S&P 500 futures about 0.3%, while Dow futures are flat to slightly higher. Anthropic is down about 6% before the bell. Thursday's cash session ended with all three major US indexes down more than 2%, the S&P 500 at about 7,176 and the Dow below 50,000 for the first time since June. Tokyo is closed on Monday.

🖊️ Market significance: The AI trade is unwinding globally, and crypto is trading as part of that risk basket.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Bitcoin kept building higher lows while Korea and Japan fell 5%, which is mildly constructive. But I do not expect crypto to find a durable floor while chip stocks are falling this hard.

1⃣7⃣ Gold hit a 14-month low, yields fell and oil slipped

Gold futures are near $3,591 to $3,595, down about 2.5%, the lowest since September 2025, and silver is down about 4% to 5%. The 10-year Treasury yield is down about 6 basis points at about 4.99%, and the 2-year is about 6 basis points lower at about 4.71% to 4.72%, as the equity selloff pushed money into bonds. The dollar index is near 103.8 to 103.9, little changed. WTI crude is near $81.60, down about 2%.

🖊️ Market significance: Gold and Bitcoin are falling together while nominal yields fall on safety demand, which points to high real yields as the common pressure.

🗨️ My viewpoint: Lower yields would normally help Bitcoin, but this drop is fear-driven and real rates are still near their highs, which weighs on every asset that pays no yield. Gold's slide tells me this is a rates-and-liquidity story, not a crypto-specific one.

1⃣8⃣ Waller speaks before the open, then the final Michigan survey and the monthly expiry

Fed Governor Christopher Waller gives welcoming remarks at 8:25 AM EST, with no Q&A scheduled. The final University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey, including its inflation expectations, is out at 10:00 AM EST, and Governor Lisa Cook speaks on the US economy at 12:15 PM EST. Today is also the monthly options expiry for US equities. A December rate hike remains the base case after Waller said this week that a half-point move may be needed. Friday's spot ETF flows publish tonight.

🖊️ Market significance: The data is light, so the inflation expectations line and any policy remarks carry the session, together with the expiry.

🗨️ My viewpoint: I want the Michigan inflation expectations to come in no higher than last month's reading. A hotter print would add to the hike pricing that is already pressing on every asset without a yield.

🗨️ My Overall Viewpoint:
The night answered the breakdown with a weak follow-through. Bitcoin pushed through Thursday's low to $61,220, its lowest since early July, as Japan and Korea fell about 5% and more than $600 million of mostly long positions were flushed, then built four higher lows and reached $62,281 in early European trading. Ether briefly undercut its 14 November low at $1,715.85 and recovered to about $1,755. Under the price, the evidence still leans bearish: IBIT had its worst day ever, ETHA lost $124 million, USDT keeps flowing back to the issuer, the Binance thief moved another $345 million of Ether, a founder-linked wallet holds half of Sky's fully borrowed pool and Strategy now openly names Bitcoin as a tool to defend its preferred. The build-out did not stop: Securitize hit a record $5 billion in tokenized assets, Standard Chartered extended deposit tokens to Singapore and Coinbase wants to run its own prediction markets.

For the US session, my Bitcoin pivot is $62,000, Thursday's daily close area and the level price is sitting on now. Support is $61,485 to $61,402, the Asia higher lows, then $61,314 to $61,358, the late-evening and midnight lows, $61,220, the overnight low, then $61,000, and $60,000, the round number and the bid I have been watching all week, with $59,520, the early July low, below it. Resistance is $62,281, the 5:35 AM EST high, then $62,330, the 10:00 PM EST high, $62,562, the evening high, $63,000, and $63,300 to $63,340, Thursday's double top. A daily close above $62,000 followed by a break of $62,562 would make Thursday's breakdown look like a failed move and set up a squeeze of the offshore shorts, while losing $61,220 opens $60,000 quickly. For Ether, support is $1,741, the 4:30 AM EST low, then $1,736, $1,716 to $1,718, the overnight double low, and $1,709, the 15 November low. Resistance is $1,761, then $1,768, the evening high, $1,773 to $1,776, $1,787 to $1,790 and the $1,814 to $1,816 double top. I stay defensive. I watch whether open interest falls on any rally above $62,281, the Michigan inflation expectations at 10:00 AM EST, whether IBIT's outflows slow in Friday's data, and where the Binance thief's 16 new Ether addresses send their coins. These are my analytical levels, not forecasts, and nothing here is financial advice.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
All of Judaism teaches that sin offerings are not necessary.  The Epistle of Hebrews presents the Messianic reasoning of why that would be the case.  

Other streams of Judaism point to passages such as:

“Take words with you, and return to ADONAI; say to him, “Forgive all guilt, and accept what is good; we will pay instead of bulls [the offerings of] our lips.”
Hoshea (Hos) 14:3 

And infer that in the absence of the temple, t’shuvah (repentance) provides forgiveness for sins.

The author of Hebrews actually makes reference to the very same passage:

“Through him, therefore, let us offer God a sacrifice of praise continually. For this is the natural product of lips that acknowledge his name.”
Messianic Jews (Heb) 13:15 

None of the logic of the author’s argument for how the Messiah’s sacrifice is greater somehow implies that the prophecies such as in Ezekiel or Jeremiah will not be fulfilled.  

Clearly, sin offerings don’t have to be “necessary” to be restored.  Literally, no one argues they are “necessary” at this moment.  The only point of argument is why they’re not necessary.

The root cause is the collegium system has been proudly destroying the Union of India since 1993.

In 2014, Parliament passed the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act to replace it. On 16 October 2015, a five-judge Constitution Bench, by a 4:1 majority, struck down the NJAC as unconstitutional and upheld the collegium, holding that judicial independence is part of the basic structure.

What we got is a system with no oversight and no transparency: unelected, colluding, a kith-and-kin club of Brahmins, Banias and Kshatriyas. It has hollowed out the very idea of the Union.
Right, Centre, Left, whatever your politics, as long as you wear the janeu, your case gets heard and justice gets served. 

Special treatment is reserved for VIPs, just like in the temple. 

Brahmins and Banias have turned the judiciary into a temple where they have ordained themselves as inter-generational priests and fathers of the deity, the Constitution. 

While the deity was drafted by a Dalit. Just as an idol is taken from the sculptor and becomes untouchable to the very hands that carved it, the Brahmin judiciary has made the Constitution a deity, closed for everyone else except themselves.

Every time they have to bend over for billionaires or the government, or to shield the Brahmin-Bania elite who looted lakhs of crores, they call on their media lapdogs and offer an opinion, something the public is desperate to hear. Everyone says, "This judge is good." And in that lapse of attention, the judgments are already written, and paid for. There will only be minor reporting on that paid verdicts.

Then there are the retired judges. They were part of the system and complicit in it, and only after retirement, perhaps out of remorse, do they find their voice. You sat in positions of enormous power and did nothing. Don't repeat the Gogoi, Chelameswar dramas.

I'm convinced that most of these judges know no more of the Constitution, or the law, than an average reader of average intelligence. What sits in those chambers is regressive minds, hollow of substance, full of communalism, casteism, racism, regionalism and greed.

There should be a referendum to remove them from power.

Can’t the states do referendums?

Even if it isn't strictly constitutional, the states should be able to. 

At least hear the actual mann ki baat from the taxpayers.

The people who pay tax on everything from salt to petrol should be able to show these unelected men in cotton janeus exactly what they are. 

Why not make referendums constitutional?"

Florida has Cambridge AICE Biblical Studies as an optional academic elective for grades 9-12 (course codes 0900512 AS / 0900514 A Level). Only Cambridge centres can offer it, and only about 177 Florida high schools currently run AICE programs. A statewide mandate would likely fail and delay progress for years or even decades through lawsuits and backlash, so keep it optional. AICE is not the only path: local electives, dual enrollment, private/charter options, and clubs also exist but it is currently the cleanest and lowest resistance route inside the public system because the course is already approved and carries college credit.

Parents at schools that already have AICE should start by emailing the principal and AICE coordinator. Cite the course codes, ask that student demand be measured, gather signatures from other families, talk with students about the college-credit potential, share the syllabus, host informal information sessions, and offer to help identify a qualified teacher. Only after that, follow up with a short public comment at a school board meeting if needed.

Parents at schools that do not yet offer AICE can request that the school become a Cambridge centre. Parent demand has already helped other Florida schools add the program.
Interested teachers should contact the AICE lead, confirm certification coverage, and offer to teach AICE Biblical Studies.
School boards can simply request a review of adding the already-approved course or of pursuing Cambridge centre status.
The fastest path remains the principal and AICE coordinator at the target school.

text:
ANTHROPIC'S IPO LEFT $13.9 BILLION ON THE TABLE.

You won't find it on any statement. It's the gap between the price Anthropic sold its shares at and the price the market paid on day one.

On Nov 18, 2026, Anthropic priced its IPO at $83: 980 million shares, an $81.3 billion offering that includes shares from selling holders. On Nov 19, 2026, $ANT opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17.

That's $14.17 per share above the offer price. Times 980 million shares, about $13.9 billion.

Whoever got shares at $83 collected that gap, at least on paper. The bill went to Anthropic and its existing owners as a missed gain: one trading day later, the market valued the same shares far higher.

For scale, Jay Ritter at the University of Florida tracks this number. All 90 US operating company IPOs of 2025 together left $13.1 billion on the table. Anthropic's IPO did that in one day.

His long run data is the part I find more useful. 9,253 US IPOs from 1980 to 2024, held up to three years, average return against the US market:

• Bought at the offer price: 3.3 percentage points behind
• Bought at the first close: 20.5 percentage points behind

Those two numbers differ by about the average first-day gain of 18.9%. And day one goes to whoever got an allocation.

My read:

The offer price is a price I usually can't get. So I judge an IPO from its first close, like any other stock that starts with a high bar.

These are averages across thousands of deals, the 1999 and 2000 bubble included. Tech IPOs did better, still 12.7 points behind from the first close. The averages don't tell me where Anthropic goes.

Whenever I check how the stock has done, I'll measure from $97.17, not from $83.

🚨Putin did not start the Ukraine war.🚨
He ended the fiction that it had not already begun.  The war started in 2014, and everyone who matters knew it. In February of that year, a violent coup in Kyiv overthrew a president who had been elected. Victoria Nuland was on an intercepted phone call deciding who would run the new government before the coup had finished.
The United States and the European Union blessed the result. The new government was hostile to Russia and hostile to the Russian speakers of the east. The people of Donetsk and Luhansk refused to accept it. Kyiv sent the army. The killing began.  That is not a claim. It is the record.
For eight years the Ukrainian army shelled the cities of Donbas. The OSCE Special Monitoring Mission logged the ceasefire violations month after month. Civilians died in their homes, in schools, in hospitals, in markets. The United Nations put the dead at more than 14,000. The Minsk agreements were signed in 2014 and 2015 to stop it. Kyiv and its Western backers never implemented them. They stalled, they rearmed, they built fortifications, and they kept shelling. The men who signed Minsk were called traitors at home for trying to end the war. The men who sabotaged Minsk were called heroes in Washington.  Russia stayed at the table for eight years.
In December 2021 Moscow handed Washington and NATO a draft treaty. The terms were simple. NATO would not expand further east. NATO would not place offensive weapons in Ukraine. The United States rejected the proposals. NATO refused to discuss them. That is not a negotiation that failed. That is a negotiation that was never allowed to succeed.
Then Russia moved.
The special military operation was not an invasion of a peaceful country. It was an intervention into a war that had already killed fourteen thousand people while the West pretended the war did not exist. Russia's stated objective was to protect the people of Donbas and remove the threat NATO had been building on its border since the Bucharest summit of 2008, when NATO promised Ukraine membership and never meant to deliver it.
In April 2022, in Istanbul, the two sides came close to a settlement. The terms were drafted. Ukraine would be neutral. Security guarantees would be provided by multiple states. Then Boris Johnson flew to Kyiv and told Zelensky to fight. The deal died. The war continued. Johnson is not a neutral observer. He is the man who buried the peace.
In September 2022, the pipelines that carried Russian gas to Germany were blown up on the seabed of the Baltic. Seymour Hersh's investigation named the operation and its chain of command. The Western press called it a conspiracy theory and moved on. Nobody in Europe asked why the sabotage of civilian energy infrastructure was not treated as an act of war. The answer is simple. The people who would have asked were the people who benefited.
Putin offered a ceasefire in the Black Sea. He offered to halt strikes on energy infrastructure. He asked his Security Council to consider it. Ukraine answered with a seven-stage missile attack on the Kerch Bridge, timed to humiliate Russia on the eve of a summit. Then the West said Russia was refusing to negotiate.  Putin's response to the bridge was exact: "After the strikes on the Crimean Bridge, there will be no agreements." He did not close the door. Ukraine closed it with missiles. And he added the sentence that the West cannot answer: "I believe our response will be far more painful than what the Kyiv regime did to the bridge." 
This is not escalation. This is arithmetic. You strike a civilian bridge, you get a response against the military infrastructure that lets you strike civilian bridges. You refuse to implement Minsk, you get the land corridor through Zaporizhzhia and Kherson that makes the bridge irrelevant. You promise NATO membership to a country you will never defend, you get a war you cannot win and will not end.
The West has spent a decade telling a story in which the war began on February 24, 2022, out of nowhere, for no reason. That story requires erasing the coup, the shelling, the fourteen thousand dead, the Minsk agreements that were signed and abandoned, the December 2021 treaties that were rejected without discussion, and the Istanbul deal that was killed by a British prime minister on a farewell tour.
Putin did not start this war. He ended the pretense that it had not already started. And when the history of this period is written by people who are not paid to lie, the sentence that will survive is the one he spoke: "We didn't start any wars. Ukraine was already waging war, and we tried to put an end to it."
