11.20 US Stocks Morning Report

Futures are lower this morning. We continue to sell off after yesterday's very ugly reversal to the downside.

- Dow Jones futures: not so bad, down about 150–170 points.
- Nasdaq and tech have taken all the pressure; Nasdaq futures are down another 500 points.
- The Qs (QQQ) traded down to 633 in the pre-market.
- Anthropic, after yesterday's world-record-setting IPO, is getting hit this morning, down nearly 10%.
- Gold was ugly overnight, down 2%. A few of you asked about a target. I said 315, and I thought we'd talk about it in a few weeks. We're almost there already. That's how ugly things are.
- Bitcoin has yet to undercut the lows from the other weekend, but it's slowly coming back into the 60,000–61,400 area.

What Matters Right Now: Feeling Safe and Prepared

I could give you a bunch of upgrades and downgrades, but that's really not what's important. What's important is that you feel safe and comfortable. In other words, you need to be able to deal with the action ahead, know what to do to stay safe, and also know how to take advantage of opportunity. So I'm going to do my best right now to tell you how to do that.

1. Have Capital — No All-Ins

The first thing is to have capital. What I mean by that is you can't be all in. You just can't, because we're not at levels that are so investable or tradable that they warrant it, and there could be another 5% or 10% to go. First and foremost: no all-ins here.

2. Take the Loss If You're Wrong

Second, most of you have done very well. The last couple of days have sucked. I was thinking about how pissed off I was, really since yesterday afternoon, with that scalp. I asked myself why I was so pissed off, and I think it's because I had been so disciplined, and then yesterday I lost that discipline after weeks of really being on top of things. It was frustrating.

So I want you to use me as an example. If you're wrong, just take a loss. When I say take a loss if you're wrong, I mean you can always buy the same stock back, sometimes 10% lower. In my case, had I not sold the Qs... I don't even want to say how much lower they are now. They're about 15 points lower. The point is: take a small loss. You'll be okay. That's the name of the game.

Sentiment and the Expected Bounce

Moving on. We see the VIX spiking. We see sentiment very depressed. I won't say all-time lows; that's exaggerated, and actually we're not near all-time lows, but it's pretty extreme. The Fear & Greed indicator is getting pretty low (or pretty high, depending on which one you look at). Either way, it's significant.

It's such that I expect a dead cat bounce, or let's just call it a vicious bear market rally. The only question is from where.

Today is Friday, and it's options expiration. A lot of people like to say markets don't bottom on a Friday, and I say, who believes that crap? Except when you're in a bear market and everyone is scared shitless. So there's a good chance we can't bottom today, because a lot of people, especially retail, don't want to buy even more going into the weekend. So you have to wonder whether the turn comes on Monday or Tuesday. And by the way, that turn isn't the end of the bear market per se. It will be a tradable turn.

So my thought is we probably get a bounce today, much like the one we got this morning. The Qs traded to the previous low at 635–637, we rallied toward 640, and now we're back down again. We could get that sort of rally. But a durable rally, something significant enough to trade off of or lighten up into, may not come until Monday, just because of the dynamics of the week. It's Friday, and people are going to be scared going into the weekend.

When I Become an Investor

As for the fear: I could talk about valuation, but that's not what you should really be thinking about. People have been talking about valuation on Micron for the last 400 points. But there does come a point where investors step up and say, okay, whether it's NVIDIA or Micron, I'm going to invest here. This doesn't make sense to me, and I'm willing to be down in order to be an investor.

I get to that point, and here's that level for me. I've been telling you this level for a while: I said at 637 I start to get excited, and I become an investor in the low 600s. That's kind of where we are.

My Plan: Stick With a Few Names

My plan is to stick with just a few names that really encompass most stocks:

- The Qs (QQQ) and TQQQ.
- The SOX, once we get low enough. I've been trading it for 30 years, and it really does offer great risk/reward at certain areas. We're getting there, and we can do it through SOXL.
- NVIDIA, because as messy as it is, it's as deeply oversold as it's been in decades.
- I may even look at gold — not here, but another 10 points lower.

On the second tier, if you've had a great few months: NBIS (Nebius) is getting to a level where, if you're strictly technical and not thinking about the bear market or about buying quality over second- and third-tier companies, NBIS looks like a buy at 85.

Moving on. I really mean it when I say you just need three or four stocks. You don't need 10. They're all going to trade together. You only need the best in breed.

So I'll also be looking at Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan if they pull back enough. Around 3 or 4 a.m., if you look up above, I gave you some of those levels. I don't remember them exactly offhand: Goldman is in the low 800s, something like 810; JPM would be 300. All of a sudden we can become investors again, and investing is fun. You can make a lot of money. I just don't think we're quite there yet, though some of my favorite names are getting there.

What You Should Do

So here's what you do. Take a deep breath. Look at the work you've done over the past few weeks and the past few months. Most of you can say: yeah, it's a little scary, but you know what, I'm actually in pretty good shape. It's not nice to compare yourself to others, but in this case, if you're a little fearful, go look out there. You're in good shape.

Why do I say that? Because you're going to have to suck it up, and at some point, press buy. We may get a rally today, but we're not at the real bottom yet. Let me explain what I'm looking for.

Technicals: RSI

The SPY is at a 29 RSI. Sentiment is very low, but in the Qs we keep getting these snapback rallies. We were above the 200-day just recently, so the RSI there isn't that low. I'm going to ask some of my friends here to pull up an oscillator reading so we can look at it. But overall, I think we can get to the mid or low 20s on RSI, which takes us to that 20% correction, another 10 or 20 points lower.

The Biggest Mistakes Happen in the Last Innings

This may be the most important part of what I'm going to tell you. So often the greatest mistakes are made in the last innings, the eighth or ninth, in both bull markets and bear markets.

In other words, you're trying to short something and you're just a few hours or a few days too soon. Notably, a lot of people did that in 2000: they got wiped out, and six months later the market got crushed. In bear markets, it's time to buy, but in that last 5% or 10% of the move you're early, and you don't have liquidity when you need it.

So think of it this way:

- Don't be a hero. Make sure you have capital on hand for an ugly Monday.
- Ask questions. Don't guess if you really don't know what you're doing. Most of you do, of course.
- Don't go buy a bunch of $5 small-cap stocks. When the market rallies, they won't even notice, because they don't care.

Closing Thoughts

I'm here to help, but I've got to go deal with some personal things. I really just came on to give you my serious thoughts, because I know there will be serious opportunity. But you won't have a shot at that opportunity if you think you know the low and go all in.

I very rarely think I know, and when I do, it screws me up. Like yesterday, when I thought the Qs weren't going to pull back that much. So don't think you know the low, because none of us do.

I do hope you're comfortable, and by comfortable I mean prepared. In fact, being uncomfortable will make you money. So when I say comfortable, I simply mean prepared, feeling like you know what to do. We can actually make a lot of money given the situation; the key is to be around to do it. I'll be on later if anything important comes up.

text:
🎵 100 SONGS WITH THE MOST INTERESTING BACKSTORIES

🐞 THE BEATLES & FRIENDS
𝟏. 'Yesterday', The Beatles 🇬🇧: Paul McCartney woke up with the melody in his head and sang it for weeks with the placeholder words 'Scrambled eggs'

𝟐. 'Let It Be': McCartney said it came from a dream in which his late mother, Mary, told him to 'let it be'

𝟑. 'Hey Jude': McCartney wrote it to comfort John Lennon's 5-year-old son Julian during his parents' divorce; it began as 'Hey Jules'

𝟒. 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds': Lennon said the title came from a drawing by little Julian of a classmate named Lucy, not from LSD

𝟓. 'Help!': Lennon later said it was a genuine cry for help at the height of Beatlemania

𝟔. 'Strawberry Fields Forever': named after Strawberry Field, a Salvation Army children's home near Lennon's childhood home in Liverpool

𝟕. 'Eleanor Rigby': a gravestone with that very name stands in St Peter's churchyard in Woolton, where Lennon and McCartney first met; McCartney says any link was subconscious

𝟖. 'Blackbird': McCartney has said it was inspired by the civil rights struggle in the US in 1968

𝟗. 'Something': George Harrison's love song, widely linked to his then-wife Pattie Boyd

𝟏𝟎. 'Layla', Derek and the Dominos: Eric Clapton poured his love for Pattie Boyd, then married to his friend Harrison, into it; the title comes from the Persian tale of Layla and Majnun 🇬🇧

𝟏𝟏. 'Wonderful Tonight': Clapton wrote it in 1976 while waiting for Boyd, by then his partner, to get ready for a party

text:
THE PAYPAH 058 | November 20, 2026
Information cutoff: 6:15 a.m. Central (CST)

The market gave Anthropic a strong first day and kept selling the companies around it. Friday’s problem is bigger than one debut: softer factory orders are arriving with more widespread cost increases.

The listing won; the wider trade didn’t
Anthropic finished its November 19 debut at $97.17, 17.1% above its $83 offer price. The S&P 500 still fell 2.02%. At 3:57 a.m. Central Friday, Reuters had E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures down 1.63% and E-mini S&P 500 futures down 0.76%. A recovery across chip and cloud shares would say more about confidence in AI returns than another move in one newly listed company.
https://t.co/YXGLZSge8o
https://t.co/a8T4WlFDA9

Fewer orders, broader cost pressure
The Philadelphia Fed’s November manufacturing survey showed general activity falling from 20.9 to 6.3 and new orders from 4.3 to −0.4. Prices paid rose from 43.2 to 58.2. These are seasonally adjusted diffusion indexes: the share reporting increases minus decreases. They measure breadth, not output growth or price inflation. Persistent weak orders alongside broader cost increases could squeeze margins. One regional survey does not establish a national downturn.
https://t.co/jpHnEQD2MR

Watch continuing claims, too
Advance, seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims rose 1,000 to 203,000 in the week ended November 14. Continuing claims, which lag a week, rose 70,000 to 1.763 million in the week ended November 7. A sustained climb in continuing claims could suggest slower job-finding; one weekly jump needs confirmation.
https://t.co/xxoKnCyt8H

Oil is still counting cargoes
Reuters put January WTI crude-oil futures at $82.20 a barrel at 5:45 a.m. Central. It reported roughly prewar crude shipments through Hormuz alongside fresh Houthi threats against Saudi Red Sea ports. Continued flows would support expectations of a surplus; verified interruptions to loadings or shipping would challenge them. A threat and a counted supply loss are different evidence.
https://t.co/8FXZzGIBDS

Our read: Michigan’s final November consumer survey, due at 9:00 a.m. Central, adds a check on household inflation expectations. If two-year Treasury yields ease while Nasdaq-100 futures keep lagging S&P 500 futures, the question of returns on AI spending deserves more weight. Selling that spreads beyond tech alongside rising inflation expectations would point to a wider problem.
https://t.co/CFIZ9udH15

TWO DIFFERENT GAME PLANS, ONE DECK.

Umbreon and Pidgeot make for an interesting B-tier combination that covers both early and late-game threats.

Umbreon applies early pressure with a fast 80 damage attack against Basic Pokémon, while Pidgeot takes over later with 120 damage against Evolution Pokémon. The idea is simple: let Umbreon control the early game, then bring in Pidgeot once your opponent has evolved their board.

With two Blue's Provocations, you also get some interesting board control options, while Ditto offers an optional tech choice that lets you copy your opponent's attacks.

The deck is surprisingly energy-efficient, with both main attackers requiring just one Energy per attack.

Would you run Ditto in this list, or cut it for another card? And do you think this combination has what it takes to compete with the top-tier decks?

text:
There's two strategies I will offer here to fill any emotional hole. They complement each other. And they both work reliably, because they are internal, they are actually under your control.

Let's apply them both to the earlier example.

1. "Assume Success"

Rewind to the morning of. You wake up with a need to be liked. You search for who can deliver that to you. You think of Boss and Cutie. 

Pause. What are you assuming here? You've assumed that Boss and Cutie don't like you. That's why you're trying to give them a reason to like you. But is it true? How do you know? Do you have direct access to their mind, or are you taking the liberty to decide on their behalf how much they like you? Here's the answer: you are. Because you have no such connection to how they actually feel about you. 

So what if instead, you decided that it's a fact that they absolutely love you, based on the exact same lack of justification whatsoever? If you were to roleplay a reality in which that was the operating principle, how would things naturally play out?

See how that works? You can just decide how other people feel about you. Because "how they feel about you" is totally disconnected from how they actually feel about you. It's all in your head. If it's all in your head, you can decide how they feel about you. You've been deciding the whole time that they don't like you. So you can just decide that they do on equally irrational grounds, and just live in that reality instead as long as it serves you. And it will, because either way, it's a self-fulfilling prophecy. Focus on what you want to see more of.

You can do this with anything and you can turn it up to the max.

Decide everyone is your friend already. Decide every woman loves you and would have sex with you, if she could. Decide your boss thinks you're competent and wants to promote you. Decide everyone you meet knows it in their bones that you're valuable, valid, worthy. 

Decide for everyone, all of the time, that you are maximum good.

And what happens? You stop needing to prove it. Huge weight lifted. Fear, lifted. So you start acting authentically, not trying. This is what enables the fulfillment of the prophecy.

text:
Total ignorance on full display anytime Mamdani blovitates:

"DealBook founder Andrew Ross Sorkin pressed Mamdani on the math behind his plan for city-run grocery stores. How could a business that typically operates on profit margins of just one to four percent afford to offer 30 percent discounts on major food items? And how would the subsidies needed to cover the shortfall affect competing supermarkets?

Mamdani’s response offered a political rationale rather than a financial explanation. If we deem something necessary for people to live, he argued, it becomes “necessary” for government to support and subsidize it.

"I take a step back and I think about when society deems something necessary for the public, then we subsidize its creation and its operation," Mamdani said. "We know that so much of what we rely on from the public sector is not being paid for at price, whether it be the subway or a public school or a library or sanitation. We have determined this is necessary. And when I think about what is necessary for a dignified life in New York City and anywhere, frankly, it is very easy to come back to food because you cannot live without it."

But notice several things. First, even the services he cites already struggle to deliver quality at a reasonable cost. Second, the American founding did not see government as responsible for providing a “dignified life.” Our Constitution emphasizes limits on what government can do and protections for individual liberty, negative rights. Progressives, in the tradition of Woodrow Wilson and FDR, champion positive rights, which require government to provide goods and services.

While negative rights protect liberty, autonomy, and help to prevent tyranny, positive rights by definition require a larger government with more control over individuals' lives, the power to take from some to provide for others. A bastardization of what the Founding Father fought for."

text:
GOOD MORNING, EVERYONE. HAPPY FRIDAY! ☕📉

Today, I want to talk about something more important than charts, predictions, or profits: HUMILITY.

I’ll start with myself: I got it wrong.

I did not anticipate such a direct selloff toward potentially sub-$700 levels on $SPY without a meaningful rebound first. And I suspect many serious traders and technical analysts didn’t either.

Look at today’s $SPX options leaderboard. Strikes around 6,900 are already attracting significant volume. This morning’s apparent phantom print near $695 on $SPY adds another interesting data point. Neither confirms where we’re headed, but both deserve attention.

Could we be forming a larger head-and-shoulders pattern? Could another 50–80 points of downside eventually materialize, filling remaining gaps?

Possibly. Nobody knows. And that’s precisely the lesson.

Markets have an extraordinary ability to make us feel invincible, especially when making money becomes easy.

That’s where psychology takes over.

Overconfidence. Confirmation bias. Loss aversion. The disposition effect. Sunk-cost thinking.

We convince ourselves we’re right. We average down because we refuse to admit we’re wrong. We hold losers hoping they’ll recover. We mistake a bull market for personal genius.

And sometimes, we follow self-proclaimed gurus whose subscription revenue is more dependable than their trading performance.

The market doesn’t owe us a rebound. It doesn’t owe us our money back. It owes us absolutely nothing.

I learned that lesson painfully during the dot-com bubble. I lost substantial money, but gained something far more valuable: respect for risk.

And I see a new generation learning similar lessons today.

I believe deeply in AI and technological progress. But a revolutionary technology does not automatically make its stocks good investments.

Innovation is not valuation. Revenue is not profit. Hype is not free cash flow.

A company can change the world while its shareholders lose fortunes.

And a stock down 70% needs to rise 233% just to break even. Some will recover. Many never will.

That’s why distinguishing durable, cash-generating businesses from speculative promises matters more than ever. Even excellent companies can fall dramatically, but their underlying economics give investors something real to evaluate.

If you’re an investor, this correction may create opportunities. But not necessarily in the same stocks that destroyed your capital.

If you’re a trader, remember that survival comes before profitability.

The hardest part of trading isn’t making money when everything is going up.

It’s keeping that money when everything stops going your way.

I’ve seen accounts make thousands, hundreds of thousands, even millions.

My question is simple: How many still have it?

And here’s an even more important question:

What will you do differently in the next bull market?

Real professionals don’t build their identities around being bulls or bears. They adapt to changing conditions, manage exposure, hedge when appropriate, and understand that sometimes the best position is no position at all.

Delta neutrality isn’t a requirement for every strategy, but the principle is powerful: Don’t become emotionally married to a direction.

Protect your financial capital. Protect your emotional capital. Protect your ability to come back tomorrow.

Because the market will offer new opportunities.

The question is whether you’ll still have the capital, discipline, and clarity to take advantage of them.

So this Friday, instead of asking who’s right, who’s bearish, or who’s bullish, ask yourself:

What did this correction teach me? And what am I actually going to change?

That’s a conversation worth having.

Respect the market. Respect the risk. Respect the work.

Stay humble. Stay disciplined. Stay in the game.

Happy Friday, everyone. 🙏

text:
Musk: Losing Jensen Is Like Losing Michael Jordan

Elon Musk compared Jensen Huang’s exit from NVIDIA to a George R.R. Martin script: the central character suddenly disappears.

At the Nov. 18 DealBook Summit, Musk said he would hire Huang, though Huang was not looking for a job. Musk said they had spoken privately, but whether they discussed a job was unclear.

Fans know the pattern: Ned Stark, then the Red Wedding. The shock comes from losing the character they had built their expectations around.

Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993 and led it for 33 years. On Nov. 12, the company announced his resignation as CEO, president and director, with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. It followed his admission of an affair, amid national-security and chip-export investigations involving unproven intelligence allegations.

On Nov. 17, Huang offered to return if the board judged it best for the company, employees and shareholders. Chairman Harvey Jones said the board had unanimously accepted his resignation and did not intend to reinstate him.

By Nov. 18, a petition had passed 200,000 signatures, including 10,111 people identifying themselves as current employees. Musk signed too. The employee affiliations were self-reported.

Musk’s other analogy was taking Michael Jordan off a winning Chicago Bulls team. He argued that nobody could truly replace Huang, whose work spanned supply chains, technology and staff loyalty. He described Huang’s decades of supplier relationships, built through visits to Korea and Taiwan and street-food meals. Musk also cited handshake commitments he trusted, and employees who stayed despite better offers elsewhere.

That influence is hard to hand over with an address book. Yet appointing the CEO remains the board’s decision.

Musk described two routes back: a board reversal, or shareholders changing the board through formal procedures—the latter, he said, is rare.

NVIDIA reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion on Nov. 17, up 103% year over year.

To me, the Game of Thrones comparison captures the shock of losing the person everyone expected at the center. The board now has to show it can sustain NVIDIA’s supply chain, team, customer relationships and technical direction without its founder. Can it keep the story going?

Commemorations
Forefeast of the Entry into the Temple of the Most Holy Theotokos
Commemorated on November 20
Today we celebrate the Forefeast of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos into the Temple, and tomorrow is the Feast Day itself. A Forefeast is one or more days preceding certain major holidays, in order to prepare the faithful for the celebration of the actual Feast Day. In the Services, hymns describing the festive event are sung.

According to Tradition, the righteous Joachim and Anna, the parents of the Virgin Mary, vowed  to dedicate their child to God. When the girl was three years old, her parents brought her to the Temple at Jerusalem holding candles and singing Psalms.

Psalm 44/45: 10-17 foreshadows this event:

"Hear, O daughter, and see, and incline your ear; forget also your people and your father’s house. Because the king has desired your beauty; for he is your Lord. And the daughter of Tyre shall adore with gifts; the rich of the people of the land shall supplicate your countenance. All her glory is that of the daughter of the king of Esebon, robed as she is golden fringed garments, in embroidered clothing; virgins shall be be brought to the king after her, her fellows shall be brought to you. They shall be brought with gladness and exaltation; they shall be led into the king's temple. Instead of your fathers children are born to you; you shall make them princes over all the earth. They shall make mention of your name from generation to generation; therefore shall the nations shall confess you for ever, even forever and ever

She was met by the priests of the Temple and the High Priest Zachariah himself. With no help from anyone else, the girl walked up fifteen steps. Zachariah, the father of Saint John the Baptist, took the Virgin Mary into the Holy of Holies: the most sacred place in the Temple, where she remained until at the age of twelve, when she was betrothed to Saint Joseph. No one could enter there except the High Priest, who entered alone once a year (on the Day of Atonement) to offer the blood of sacrificial animals "for himself, and for the errors of the people" (Hebrews 9:7). But Zachariah was given an extraordinary inspiration for his action. After all, the Virgin herself was to become the Holy of Holies, a living temple, bearing in her womb the Savior of the world.

text:
Today’s Reading: Genesis 10–12 & Matthew 4
At Babel, humanity grasped for a self-made name and fractured into seventy scattered nations. Centuries later in the Judean wilderness, the true Seed of Abraham refused every shortcut to glory—defeating Satan with the written Word and launching the light that gathers the nations back into one unified household under God.
Timeline & Covenant Setting
Genesis 10–12 (Pre-cross, dispersion of nations to inaugural Abrahamic Covenant): Moves directly from the post-Flood Table of Nations and the judgment at Babel (Gen. 10–11) into God’s unilateral election of Abram (Gen. 12:1–3)—four centuries before the Sinaitic administration at Mount Sinai.
Matthew 4 (Pre-cross, public inauguration of Messiah’s kingdom mission): Immediately follows Jesus’ Spirit-anointing at the Jordan (Matt. 3:16–17). Before preaching a sermon or calling a disciple, the sinless Son enters the wilderness to stand where Adam, Abram, and national Israel stumbled.
1. The Shadow: Scattered Nations, Unilateral Grace & a Stumbling Patriarch (Genesis 10–12)
Defying the Creation Mandate at Babel (Gen. 10:1–11:9): Genesis 10 traces seventy foundational nations branching from Noah’s sons (Japheth, Ham, Shem), including Nimrod’s early imperial kingdom at Babel in Shinar (Gen. 10:8–10). Genesis 11:1–9 explains why they separated: instead of filling the earth as commanded (Gen. 1:28; 9:1, 7), unified humanity baked brick and bitumen to build a city and tower so they could "make a name [šēm] for ourselves" and prevent dispersion (Gen. 11:4). With deliberate judicial irony, YHWH "came down" (yārad, Gen. 11:5) to inspect their sky-reaching tower, confused (bālal) their single speech, and scattered them across the earth—dismantling totalitarian rebellion before it could replicate pre-Flood corruption.
The Unilateral Call of Abram (Gen. 11:10–12:3): Immediately after scattering the nations, Moses narrows Shem’s genealogy down to Terah and Abram in Ur (Gen. 11:10–32). God calls Abram out of idolatry (Josh. 24:2) with a sevenfold covenant promise—granting by sovereign grace what Babel tried to seize by pride: "I will make your name great... and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed" (Gen. 12:2–3), targeting the exact nations scattered in Genesis 10–11.
Altars in Canaan vs. Stumbling in Egypt (Gen. 12:4–20): Entering Canaan, Abram builds altars at Shechem and Bethel, calling upon the name of the Lord in pagan territory (Gen. 12:7–8). Yet when severe famine strikes the promised land (Gen. 12:10), Abram descends into Egypt without consulting God and resorts to deception over Sarai to protect himself—jeopardizing the promised seed. Only YHWH’s direct intervention through plagues delivers Sarai and rescues Abram, proving from the start that the Abrahamic covenant stands on God’s faithfulness, not human perfection.
2. The Substance: The Faithful Son & Light to the Gentiles (Matthew 4)
Defeating Satan Where Adam, Abram & Israel Fell (Matt. 4:1–11): Led by the Spirit (hypo tou Pneumatos, Matt. 4:1) into the wilderness for forty days—mirroring Israel’s forty years in the desert (Deut. 8:2)—Jesus faces three assaults targeting His divine Sonship ("If you are the Son of God...", Matt. 4:3, 6):
Sustenance (Matt. 4:3–4): Tempted to turn stones into bread after forty days of hunger, Jesus refuses to distrust the Father’s provision, quoting Deuteronomy 8:3 ("Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God"). Where Abram compromised during famine in Egypt (Gen. 12:10–13) and Israel murmured over manna (Exod. 16), Christ stands firm.
Spectacle (Matt. 4:5–7): Satan twists Psalm 91:11–12 out of context, urging Jesus to leap from the temple pinnacle. Jesus exposes the distortion with Deuteronomy 6:16 ("You shall not put the Lord your God to the test"), recalling Israel’s unbelief at Massah (Exod. 17:1–7).
Sovereignty (Matt. 4:8–11): Offered all the kingdoms of the world and their glory in exchange for bowing to Satan—a cross-less shortcut to global rule—Jesus commands Satan to depart using Deuteronomy 6:13 ("You shall worship the Lord your God and Him only shall you serve").
The Abrahamic Blessing Breaks Out in Galilee (Matt. 4:12–17): Following John’s arrest, Jesus settles in Capernaum in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali—explicitly fulfilling Isaiah 9:1–2 as a great light dawning in "Galilee of the Gentiles" (Matt. 4:15–16). As Galatians 3:8, 16 confirms, Christ Himself is the singular Seed (sperma) of Abraham through whom blessing reaches the scattered nations of Genesis 10–12—incorporating Jew and Gentile alike into one unified redeemed people (ekklēsia, Eph. 2:14–16).
Unhesitating Allegiance to the King (Matt. 4:18–25): Preaching "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand" (Matt. 4:17), Jesus calls Simon Peter, Andrew, James, and John. Immediately (eutheōs, Matt. 4:20, 22) they leave their nets, boats, and father to follow Him, while crowds from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan gather around His authoritative teaching and healing power.
3. The Plumbline for Today
Immediate Context Defeats Scriptural Distortion: Satan quoted Psalm 91 verbatim yet stripped it of its covenantal context of obedience (Matt. 4:6). Letting Scripture interpret Scripture—and refusing isolated proof-texting—is the believer’s primary safeguard against false theological systems.
Never Trade Integrity for Relief Under Famine: Scarcity and pressure reveal what we actually trust. Abram’s descent into Egypt (Gen. 12:10–13) warns against self-protective compromise, while Christ’s wilderness fast (Matt. 4:2–4) proves that living by God’s Word outlasts every earthly shortage.
Reject Cross-Less Shortcuts to Influence: Both Babel (Gen. 11:4) and Satan’s third temptation (Matt. 4:8–9) offer a great name and worldly dominion apart from submission to God. True authority belongs solely to the obedient Son (Matt. 28:18; Phil. 2:8–11).
Build Altars, Not Monuments: Wherever Abram pitched his tent in Canaan, he erected an altar to the Lord (Gen. 12:7–8); when Jesus called in Galilee, fishermen abandoned lesser pursuits immediately (Matt. 4:20, 22). Faithful stewardship anchors every household first in the worship and lordship of Christ.

Union of India, where the court observed that a mosque is not an "essential part of the practice of the religion of Islam" because namaz (prayer) can be offered anywhere, even in the open. [1, 2, 3]
•Contrast with Consecrated Temples. In his court petitions (such as his 2016 Ram Temple Writ Petition), Swamy argues that a consecrated Hindu temple (Prana Pratishtha) is the literal abode of a deity and cannot be moved, whereas a mosque is simply a community hall or building that can be relocated without violating a Muslim's fundamental right to pray under Article 25 of the Constitution. [1, 2, 3]
•Precedents in Islamic Nations. To support his claim that mosques do not hold permanent, immovable sanctity, Swamy points out that countries like Saudi Arabia routinely demolish or relocate mosques to build roads and public infrastructure. [1, 2]

MY BELOVED, I GREET YOU ALL IN THE NAME OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST.

First, I want to give all the glory, honour and adoration to God Almighty for everything He has been doing in our lives and for the things He continues to do across the world.

When I speak about what God is doing in the world, I speak from a heart filled with gratitude. This year, God has granted me the honour of receiving two international world awards, and this is one of them. Whenever I look at this award, I am reminded that the God we serve is able to take an ordinary man and use him to touch nations.

I dedicate this honour to our Lord Jesus Christ, who sits on the throne. I am nothing without Him. Every recognition, every opportunity and every testimony belongs to Him alone.

When I travelled to Israel and had the opportunity to meet with 73 global prayer leaders, I could only bow my head and give God the glory. I never imagined that people from different nations would one day come to me and say, "Rev. Dachomo, we have been watching you on social media. Please pray for our government and our nations."

My beloved, this is not the work of man. This is the hand of God.

I remember when I continued praying for the President of Nigeria despite the controversies surrounding the Muslim-Muslim ticket. Some people accused me of being paid by the government. But let me make this clear: I have not received a single kobo from the Federal Government for my prayers or advocacy.

I pray because I believe in the power of prayer. I pray because I love my country. I pray because the Bible teaches us to pray for those in authority, regardless of our personal differences.

Many people have offered to support me personally, and I appreciate everyone who has stood with me. I will never deny those who have helped me. Among those who have supported me are Miller, the Plateau State Government and others whose kindness I will always appreciate. Without the help and kindness of people, there were moments when survival itself would have been difficult.

When I travelled to Israel, people from the United States and Europe approached me, saying, "Rev. Dachomo, we have been seeing you everywhere on social media. Many people want to support you."

My response was simple: Tell the truth, because the truth shall set you free.

My beloved, I have faced criticism, accusations, insults and threats because of the things I stand for. There were times when some people wished to see me silenced. Some even imagined that one day they would hear that Rev. Dachomo was dead.

But I am still standing, not because I am stronger than my enemies, but because God has sustained me.

I have made mistakes like every other human being, but I have always desired to honour God with my life. Even in my marriage, I have chosen to remain faithful to my wife because I believe my body is the temple of the Holy Spirit.

I want the world to understand something: recognition must never make us forget the One who gave us the opportunity to be recognised. Awards may come and go, applause may fade, and people may forget our names, but our relationship with God must remain our greatest treasure.

OUR BIBLE READING TODAY IS TAKEN FROM LUKE 7:7 (KJV):

"But say in a word, and my servant shall be healed."

Look at the faith of the centurion. He understood that Jesus did not need to be physically present before a miracle could happen. He believed that just one word from the Lord was enough.

My beloved, that is the kind of faith we need in this generation.

You may be facing battles that nobody knows about. You may be waiting for an opportunity, healing, financial breakthrough, restoration or an answer to your prayers. Do not give up because the God who spoke to the servant's situation is still alive today.

Never allow human rejection to make you doubt God's promises. Never allow the absence of applause to make you abandon your assignment. And never allow the blessings God gives you to make you forget the Giver.

text:
#PrinceOnThisDay - Ain’t Nothin’ Like Funky Music: F.U.N.K. Arrives via iTunes.

On 20 November 2007, Prince delivered the standalone digital single “F.U.N.K.” through iTunes under NPG Records, a pure online drop with no physical counterpart anywhere. The track, running roughly seven minutes and thirty-six seconds, originated as a vault piece tracked around 2003–early 2004 at Paisley Park Studios in Chanhassen, Minnesota. 

Engineer accounts place the initial sessions near the Musicology period; Prince later updated the lyrics and re-recorded it on 7 November 2007 before circulating it. Vocals sit in the high, helium-tinged Camille register, layered over guitar-driven funk, silky keyboards (Renato Neto), and backing from Shelby J. The result is a sly, groove-heavy response rather than a conventional single.

Context explains the timing. In September 2007 Prince’s team had pursued copyright issues involving unauthorized images and content on platforms and fan sites. Several sites formed Prince Fans United (PFU). Within days of the collective’s launch, Prince offered them a stream of the song under the temporary title PFUnk. It soon appeared as Jam of the Week on https://t.co/tr3b36XSjW and on a hastily registered https://t.co/e6gpa46UgG domain. The commercial iTunes release, retitled F.U.N.K., followed as a worldwide digital single (AAC, typically 256 kbps iTunes Plus, DRM-free). Discogs and Prince Vault confirm only these digital file versions—no catalog number beyond “none.” The single never charted and later left the store around 2012.

No physical product ever existed, so there is no packaging, jewel case, slipcase, booklet, or inlay. The sole visual is the digital cover art: Prince in a bright orange jacket with black trim, thrusting a microphone toward the viewer against a green-lit background, with bold “PRINCE F.U.N.K.” lettering. That image accompanied the iTunes listing and earlier promotional use on https://t.co/tr3b36XSjW; nothing else accompanied the file.

Lyrics lean into the moment without abandoning the groove. Lines such as “Ain’t nothin’ like funky music / To start me on my day,” “The best remedie for a basket full of lies is funk,” and the pointed “You might not like the taste / But I’m still gon’ stick your face in this funk” sit alongside a nod to the unreleased “The Grand Progression.” Fans, including those on the sites addressed, largely embraced the track as one of the stronger recent jams. It remains a non-album curiosity—never added to any official studio set—whose entire existence is digital and whose packaging is, by design, nonexistent.
@prince @PaisleyPark

text:
🚨🇨🇳 PENTAGON IN PANIC: CHINA'S MOST ADVANCED STEALTH FIGHTER J-20A GOES ‘BEAST MODE’

China’s upgraded J-20A stealth fighter appears to pair its new Chinese-built WS-15 engines with eight missiles mounted under its wings. A November 18 image may offer the first clear look at this version flying in “beast mode,” according to aviation analyst Andreas Rupprecht.

🔸 The missiles hang in pairs from four mounts, two under each wing. They resemble China’s radar-guided PL-15, an air-to-air missile designed to reach aircraft well beyond the distance at which pilots can see them.

🔸 A J-20 had already been photographed with eight missiles under its wings earlier in November. What caught Rupprecht’s eye in the newer image was the combination of that load and what he identified as the upgraded engines.

🔸 The Chinese-built WS-15 delivers more thrust than the J-20’s earlier engines. That extra power matters when a fighter carries the weight and drag of eight exposed missiles, though how much speed or range the J-20A retains with them is still an open question.

🔸 For scale, the original J-20 can carry four long-range missiles in its main bay and one short-range missile on each side. The eight weapons visible under the wings alone outnumber that entire internal load. The bay doors are closed in the image, so the total aboard is unknown.

🔸 Carrying weapons inside helps give the J-20 its radar-evading shape. Hanging missiles under the wings gives radar more surfaces to pick up, a trade-off that even a more powerful engine can’t erase.

If China clears the configuration for service, its air force could use the same fighter with its weapons tucked away for stealth or with a heavier load that gives pilots more shots before they have to return and rearm.

Does ‘Beast Mode’ make J-20A deadlier or more vulnerable?

text:
He likely reasoned that the concept of drinking milk made perfect sense; after all, humans already nursed their own offspring. 

Around 10,000 years ago, during the Neolithic period, early farmers began domesticating wild cattle for meat, hides, and labor. Slaughtering a cow provided a family with meat for a few weeks, whereas milking the animal offered food over many months without killing it. 

About 9,000 years ago, humans began turning milk into cheese, yogurt, and butter, a method that naturally breaks down lactose and preserves calories for lean months. 

Roughly 7,000 years ago, a random genetic mutation emerged in Central Europe and the Eurasian steppe, enabling adults to produce the enzyme lactase. This allowed them to consume raw milk without getting sick, a massive survival advantage. 

It took ~5,000 years for the ability to digest fresh milk to reach roughly 90% of Northern Europeans, alongside populations in East Africa and the Middle East. 

Globally, however, about 65% of adults remain lactose intolerant, a state that reflects the original human condition.

The Traditional Account: Many early Islamic sources (like the hadith collections of Bukhari and Muslim) state that Aisha was six years old at the time of her betrothal and nine when the marriage was consummated. This is the basis for the accusation.

Questionable Narration: The key hadith is traced to a single narrator, Hisham ibn Urwah, who reportedly had a poor memory in his later years.

Contradictory Evidence: Other historical reports suggest Aisha was much older. For example, she is said to have been present at the Battle of Badr (which would be impossible for a young child) and her sister Asma was reportedly 10 years older, making Aisha a teenager at the time of the marriage.

Historical Context: Slavery existed in pre-Islamic Arabia, and the Prophet Muhammad did own slaves and participate in the system, which was a reality of his time.

text:
Kazini wanted to shoot me" -- Inside the 2011 trial of Lydia Draru

When Lydia "Atim" Draru stood before the High Court in Kampala in August 2011, she confessed to killing former Army Commander Maj. Gen. James Kazini, insisting she had acted purely in self-defence.

At that stage of the trial, the prosecution had drawn first blood by succeeding in having Draru formally charged with murder rather than the lesser offence of manslaughter she had hoped for.

Draru, who had been hoping to plead to manslaughter, had shot to national notoriety nearly two years earlier, in November 2009, when she bludgeoned Maj. Gen. Kazini to death. At the time, media cameras converged on the rented house in Namuwongo where the killing occurred, capturing scenes from a crime scene that resembled a bloodbath.

In late August 2011, the same intense media scrutiny returned as High Court Judge Monica Mugenyi ruled that Draru's defence team led by Annet Mutabingwa and Musa Sembajja would have to answer to a full murder charge. Draru had sought a manslaughter plea on the grounds that she acted in self-defence after Kazini allegedly "threatened to get his gun and finish me off," hoping the lesser charge would earn her a lighter sentence, perhaps even a caution. However, State Prosecutor Fred Kakooza and his assistant, Faith Turumanya, strongly objected to the offer.

Justice Mugenyi settled the preliminary dispute by noting: "The other three ingredients have been agreed to by the accused person and these are: killing the deceased, the deceased being dead, and malice aforethought. So, let the murder charge be read for the accused to take plea."

Reading out the summary of the case, Kakooza revealed that Draru was a mistress to the deceased. On the fateful day of November 10, 2009, the two had just returned from a night out when Kazini accused her of stealing his money. A violent altercation ensued, during which Draru ran to the bathroom, picked up a hollow, silver-like metal bar, and bludgeoned Kazini to death. Draru pleaded not guilty to the murder charge and distanced herself from allegations that she had previously warned Kazini he would die at the hands of women.

Several key witnesses took the stand during those August 2011 hearings to paint a picture of the fateful night:

Scovia Toboru (Draru's niece): Toboru, whose school tuition Kazini was paying, offered an account supporting her aunt's self-defence claim. Present in the house when the quarrel erupted, she testified that she saw Kazini box her aunt on the head and slap her twice before she fled outside to seek help. "On coming back, I heard my aunt saying: 'I have killed Gen. Kazini.' She picked up her phone, rang the LC 1 area chairman, and told him to come and take her to the police," Toboru told the court.

Dr. Tadeo C. Barungi (Retired Commissioner of Police): Leading a team of eight pathologists who examined Kazini's body at the Kampala City Council mortuary hours after the incident, Barungi testified that Kazini died of extensive injuries resulting from physical trauma. Under cross-examination, he clarified that medical examiners could not definitively establish whether the wounds stemmed from a mutual fight.

Dr. Susan Nabadda: Another prosecution witness, Nabadda told the court that when she examined Draru (then 28) at the Mulago Hospital paralegal clinic, she found her to be of sound mind, noting that Draru also bore multiple injuries on her neck.

Andrew Mubiru Kizimula (Government Laboratory Analyst): Kizimula testified that DNA analysis conducted in Nairobi matched both Kazini and Draru to samples recovered from the scene.

Detective Robert Icoot (Scene of Crime Officer): Attached to Kabalagala Police Station, Icoot told the court he recovered Draru's bag inside Kazini's vehicle parked at the gate of her residence, containing Kazini's loaded revolver and an unspecified sum of US dollars. Inside the sitting room, he observed signs of a violent struggle: broken glasses, a shattered glass table, a broken portrait frame of Kazini in army uniform, a bottle of Black Label whisky, and the General's body lying on the floor.

With two prosecution witnesses remaining at the close of that week's sessions, Draru opted not to call defence witnesses, preparing instead to take the stand in her own defence before Justice Mugenyi and court assessors Ben Muhwezi and Stella Nyanzi Zziwa.

Despite the prosecution's initial success in securing a murder indictment, the trial ultimately swung in Draru's favour on the question of intent.

On September 1, 2011, Justice Monica Mugenyi acquitted Draru of murder, ruling that the state had failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that she acted with malice aforethought. Instead, the High Court found her guilty of the lesser offence of manslaughter and sentenced her to 14 years in prison, noting that the two years she had already spent on remand would be factored into her term. Although the state subsequently filed an appeal arguing that the sentence was overly lenient, the conviction and sentence stood.

Draru served her sentence at Luzira Maximum Security Prison, where she largely kept a low profile and took up hairdressing. Following statutory remission for good conduct, she was quietly released from prison in 2021 more than a decade after the high-profile killing that captivated Uganda.

text:
In 326 BC, Alexander the Great nearly destroyed his own empire by climbing a ladder.

He had defeated Darius III, conquered the Persian Empire, and marched into India. He had survived more than a decade of almost uninterupted warfare. 

Yet his closest brush with death came not against a great king or a massive army, but at the walls of an obscure fortified town. The troble began when Alexander lost patience with his own soldiers.

Not long before, his army had refused to march any farther east. Alexander turned south instead and began fighting his way through the Mallians of the Punjab. 

At one of their strongholds, the Macedonians breached the outer defenses, but the defenders withdrew into the citadel. Alexander ordered his men to scale its walls. 

Frustrated by the delay, Alexander seized a ladder and climbed it himself. He reached the battlements with only a few companions close behind. 

Below him, the soldiers rushed to follow their king, crowding onto the rungs. The ladder snapped under their weight, and Alexander was left standing above the enemy, cut off from his army.

Staying on the wall meant being shot down from every direction. So Alexander did something extraordinary. He jumped, not out of the fortress, but into it. 

Arrian presents the leap as a deliberate choice, not a fall. Alexander landed among the defenders, put his back against the wall so he could not be surrounded, and fought. 

Three men managed to follow Alexander into the fortress. Peucestas, Leonnatus, and Abreas. But Abreas was struck in the face by an arrow and killed. The remaining two fought desperately beside their king. 

The defenders recognized the chance in front of them. Alexander killed several who came within reach, so they stopped approaching and began shooting. 

An arrow punched through his armor and into his chest, apparently piercing a lung. Our sources say air and blood escaped from the wound with his breath. He kept fighting as long as he could, then collapsed. 

Peucestas and Leonnatus stood over their fallen king. Peucestas shielded Alexander with a sacred relic the Macedonians had carried since the beginning of their invasion of Asia.

In 334 BC, Alexander had visited Troy and offered sacrifices to the heroes of the Trojan War. There, he had taken a shield traditionally associated with Achilles.

Now, eight years later, the man who had spent his life modeling himself on Achilles lay dying beneath the hero's shield. 

Outside, the Macedonians were frantic. Some scrambled over the walls while others battered at the gates. 

When they finally reached Alexander, the man who had conquered the Persian Empire was lying unconscious inside a fortress most of his subjects had never heard of. 

His companions carried him out. Removing the arrow was dangerous, and he lost a great deal of blood. Rumors spread that Alexander was dead. 

The army was devastated. Without him, who would command them? How would they escape India, surrounded by peoples who might rise against them? 

Alexander eventually showed himself to his troops to prove he was alive. The men erupted in celebration. Some wept, and others reached out to touch him.

The relief concealed a terrifying reality. Alexander had conquered an empire larger than any the Greeks had ever known, but its unity still depended overwhelmingly on one man. 

When he did die in 323 BC, his generals fought over the succession and carved the empire into rival kingdoms. 

Three years earlier, the situation might have been even worse. Alexander had no son, no clear successor, and an army stranded thousands of miles from Macedon. 

Alexander had survived the armies of Persia, the deserts of Central Asia, and years of relentless war. 

Yet the empire he spent his life conquering nearly came apart because he could not wait for another ladder.

COMMANDANTS AWCN AND NWCN HOST NDC KENYA DELEGATION ON FACT-FINDING VISIT TO STUDY PROFESSIONAL MILITARY EDUCATION IN NIGERIA

The Commandant, Army War College Nigeria (AWCN), Major General Aminu Mohammed Umar, alongside his counterpart from the Naval War College Nigeria (NWCN), Rear Admiral Mohammed Adamu Muye, on 18 November 2026, received a delegation from the National Defence College (NDC), Kenya, at the AWCN Complex in Asokoro, Abuja. The visit was aimed at providing the delegation with first-hand insights into the Professional Military Education (PME) programmes of Nigeria's Services War Colleges, in preparation for the proposed establishment of a National War College in Kenya.

Speaking on behalf of the delegation, the Team Leader, Major General Richard Wambua Mwanzia, expressed appreciation to the Commandants for the warm reception and their willingness to share their wealth of experience, institutional framework and course structure. He explained that the visit was designed to understudy the organisational structures, curricula, and administrative frameworks of AWCN and NWCN as part of efforts to establish a National War College in Kenya. 

Major General Mwanzia further noted that the delegation was in Nigeria to exchange ideas and draw valuable lessons from the country's PME system, particularly the experiences of the NDC, which they had earlier visited, and the Services War Colleges. He added that the knowledge gained would contribute to developing an institutional model capable of addressing Kenya's peculiar military needs and operational leadership requirements.

In his response, the Commandant AWCN, Major General AM Umar, warmly welcomed the delegation and assured them of the Colleges' willingness to extend mentorship and institutional support towards the successful establishment of the proposed institution. He commended the delegation for selecting the Nigerian Services War Colleges as part of its fact-finding engagements, noting that the institutions had, over the years, established themselves as reputable centres for developing highly trained and competent operational-level leaders for the Nigerian Armed Forces.

The Commandant also shared insights into some of the potential challenges associated with establishing a new war college, offering practical recommendations on critical considerations for institutional development and sustainability. He particularly emphasised the strategic importance of location, explaining that proximity to resource persons, subject-matter experts, and relevant collaborating institutions could significantly enhance the effectiveness, operational efficiency, and growth of a war college.

Reaffirming the Colleges' commitment to supporting the initiative, Major General Umar further stated that they remained available to provide further guidance and assistance beyond the visit. He emphasised the importance of collaboration and the sharing of institutional experiences among Africa's military establishments, assuring the delegation that, “We can offer our advice beyond this interaction, and we are ready to offer more assistance whenever needed in the spirit of one Africa.”

Contributing to the deliberations, the Commandant NWCN, Rear Admiral MA Muye, highlighted the existing collaborative relationship among the Services War Colleges and the National Defence College Nigeria. He also underscored the critical role of the war colleges in bridging the gap between tactical and strategic levels of military education, thereby preparing military officers for higher responsibilities in operational planning, command, and leadership.

Present at the engagement were the Deputy Commandant/Director of Studies, AWCN, Brigadier General Moyosore Akin-Ojo, as well as Directors and Directing Staff from the Army and Naval War Colleges.

ARMY HEADQUARTERS DEPARTMENT OF ARMY ADMINISTRATION ANNUAL ADMINISTRATIVE INSPECTION (AAI) TEAM VISITS 1 BRIGADE NIGERIAN ARMY, GUSAU

In furtherance of the Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu’s Command Philosophy, which seeks to build a highly professional, agile, combat-effective and resilient Nigerian Army, the Army Headquarters Department of Army Administration Annual Administrative Inspection Team, led by Brigadier General AJ Ahmad, on Thursday, 19 November 2026, paid an inspection visit to Headquarters 1 Brigade Nigerian Army, Gusau.

The inspection team was received by the Acting Commander 1 Brigade, Colonel Joseph Umaru, at the Brigade Headquarters. In his remarks, the Team Leader stated that the inspection was aimed at assessing the level of administrative efficiency, ensuring compliance with established military procedures and reinforcing the culture of institutional accountability across formations. He further emphasised that commanders at all levels must cultivate a culture of doing the right thing at all times, irrespective of whether an inspection is being conducted or not.

Furthermore, Brigadier General Ahmad reiterated the COAS's 'Soldier First" mantra, stressing that the welfare of personnel must remain a top priority for all commanders. He charged commanders to maintain a high standard of discipline, exercise firm and effective command, and ensure that troops are adequately catered for, particularly in areas of medical care and general welfare. He also commended the Acting Commander 1 Brigade for his commitment to troops' welfare, with particular commendation for the attention given to their medical needs, vehicles repairs and maintenance, enhancement of security to protect lives and properties.

In his response, the Acting Commander, Colonel Joseph Umaru, expressed appreciation to the inspection team for the visit and the professional guidance offered. He assured the Team Leader that all observations and recommendations arising from the inspection had been duly noted and would be accorded the necessary attention to ensure improved administrative efficiency and operational effectiveness within the Brigade.

Highlights of the visit included an administrative briefing at Headquarters 1 Brigade, inspection of 1 Brigade Garrison, 8 Base Ammunition Depot and selected Combat Teams within the Brigade's Area of Responsibility.

The visit further provided an opportunity to assess the Brigade's administrative posture, identify areas requiring improvement and reinforce the commitment of the Nigerian Army to professionalism, accountability, discipline and effective troop welfare in line with the COAS's Command Philosophy. The visit ended on a high note with group photograph. 

YUSUF MOHAMMED
Captain
Acting Assistant Director Army Public Relations
1 Brigade Nigerian Army, Gusau
19 November 2026

Asia’s Safest and Most Unsafe Locations for the Pole Shift

Zetatalk does not publish an official ranked list of the countries. It gives criteria and location-specific comments. 

Safety is Judged Mainly By:  
•  Distance from coasts (≥100 miles inland preferred; ≥200 ft elevation to avoid tidal sloshing/tsunamis during the shift hour).  
•  Avoidance of major flood plains, rivers that will overflow massively, and areas expected to sink.  
•  Preference for older, stable rock.  
•  Distance from fault zone's and related rupture paths.  
•  Avoidance of recent volcanoes (roughly 100-mile radius) and dams that are expected to fail.  
•  The Aftertime considerations (sea-level rise of ~675 ft within ~2 years from ocean heating + polar melt; new climate/latitude; refugee pressure)

Key Zetatalk Criteria Applied to Asia

•  India: Forced under the Himalayas as the Indo-Australian Plate plunges. The entire country essentially goes under the waves during the shift hour (new South Pole location). Advice is to leave the lowlands/country entirely and head to the Himalayas (Tibet, Nepal, China, or high Indian territory such as Srinagar). Boats over India are not viable due to vortexes.

• Japan: Gains elevation (average ~150–200 ft, more in the north ~250 ft, less in the south). However, it sits at major plate junctions with severe compression, volcanoes, Pacific shortening, and tsunamis. No truly safe place; high ground away from coasts and volcanoes is relatively better, but outcomes are unpredictable. Southern islands (on the Eurasian Plate) fare somewhat better.

•  China: Inland mainland fares relatively well (higher elevation, stretch-zone rather than active mountain-building). Southern coasts lose ~20 ft of elevation and face tsunami risk from Indonesian plate sinking. Climate becomes cooler (closer to the new South Pole). Northern areas (e.g., Heilongjiang) are noted more favorably. Rivers and lowlands still flood heavily.

•  Indonesia: Fares poorly overall - low-lying, subducting, significant elevation loss (up to ~80 ft in the south), volcanoes, and flood tides from Pacific-to-Indian Ocean water movement. High mountains in Borneo are somewhat better, but survival is mostly accidental.

•  Southeast Asia: Thailand, lowland Vietnam, Cambodia, Malaysia, Philippines, and Bangladesh face severe elevation loss, drowning, tsunami, and (in the Philippines) widespread volcanic activity. Lowlands are particularly vulnerable.

•  Himalayas / Tibet / Nepal: High ground destination for those fleeing India, but subject to mountain-building and Aftertime cold near the new South Pole.

•  General: Prefer high ground well inland, older/stable rock in stretch zones, and elevations that remain above ~675 ft Aftertime sea-level rise. Avoid subduction zones, active volcanoes, and areas expected to sink.

Approximate Ranked List: Safest → Most Unsafe
(Major countries/regions; local high ground can improve odds)

Relatively Safest
1.  Mongolia - Inland, high elevation, stretch-zone older terrain; not subject to major subduction or sinking.
2.  Northern China (e.g., Heilongjiang Province and northern Neimongol) - Explicitly noted as a good migration target; solid land bridge northward, warmer Aftertime climate relative to its new position.
3.  Inland China (away from coasts and major river valleys) - Higher elevations and stretch-zone geology give better odds than most of Asia. Coasts and southern lowlands are riskier.

Moderate / Mixed 
4. Tibet / Himalayan highlands / Nepal - High ground remains above water, but mountain-building, quakes, and aftertime cold (near the new South Pole) are significant issues. Primary destination for Indians fleeing the plunge. 
5. Japan - Gains elevation, but extreme plate trauma, volcanoes, and water movement make it highly unpredictable. High inland spots are relatively better than coasts or cities like Tokyo. 
6. South Korea / Korean Peninsula - Mixed; inland/higher ground preferable to coasts. Limited specific commentary but better than pure island or sinking zones. 
7. Central Asian highlands (parts of Kazakhstan, etc., bordering Russia) - Higher elevations help, though refugee pressure and some flooding expected.

Most Unsafe 
8. Southern coastal China / lowland Vietnam / Cambodia - Elevation loss and tsunami exposure from the Indonesian plate tongue sinking. 
9. Philippines - Island chain with numerous volcanoes that will erupt, subject to over-wash, and elevation loss. 10. Thailand / Malaysia / Bangladesh lowlands - Significant drowning risk and elevation loss. 
11. Indonesia - Overall poor prognosis: low-lying, subducting, major elevation loss, volcanoes, and flood tides. High mountains in Borneo are the least-bad option. 
12. India - Explicitly plunges under the Himalayas and goes under the waves. Survival requires leaving the country for high Himalayan ground before the shift hour.

Practical Takeaway from the Material

Inland high ground in Mongolia and northern/inland China offers the relatively best odds in Asia. The Himalayas serve as a last refuge for those in India, but with major trade-offs. Japan gains elevation yet faces extreme trauma. India, Indonesia, and lowland Southeast Asia are among the most hazardous regions described anywhere. Coasts, river valleys, and areas expected to sink should be avoided. Check specific elevations against the ~200 ft (Pole Shift-hour) and ~675 ft (Aftertime) guidelines.

Key Zetatalk Criteria Applied to Russia

•  Aftertime Sea-Level Rise (~675 ft): Most of Russia is lowland. Vast areas of Siberia and European Russia will flood within months to 2 years after the shift. Survivors on low ground must migrate (often by boat) as waters rise.

•  Urals as Primary Sanctuary: The Ural Mountains will become an island surrounded by rising waters. Russian government/elite bunkers are described as planned there.

•  Eastern Highlands: Mountains in eastern/Far East Russia are sparsely populated, remain above water, and are expected to have a favorable climate with ocean access. Early migration advised.

•  Western/Central Lowlands: Moscow and environs will be inundated (no permanent elevation drop, but full flooding from sea-level rise). St. Petersburg and similar areas face shift-hour tidal issues plus permanent inundation.

•  Other Factors: New seaway ripping northward from the Pakistan region toward the Urals. Northern coasts need extra caution due to flat terrain and water pooling. Avoid river bottoms. Kamchatka has volcanic activity. General advice: high ground or boats if not already near highlands.

Approximate Ranked List: Safest → Most Unsafe
(Major regions / federal subjects groupings; local high ground improves odds)

Relatively Safest
1.  Ural Mountains region (e.g., parts of Sverdlovsk Oblast, Chelyabinsk Oblast, Perm Krai, Bashkortostan near the range) — Explicitly described as the main sanctuary; becomes an island. Elite bunkers planned here (non-elites advised to stay clear of those areas).
2.  Eastern / Far East highlands (e.g., mountainous parts of Yakutia/Sakha, Magadan Oblast, Amur Oblast, Khabarovsk Krai, mountainous areas west of Verkhoyansk / south of Kolyma) — High ground remains above water; good aftertime climate and fishing access; sparsely populated.
3.  Southern mountain areas (e.g., Altai Republic, parts of the Caucasus in southern federal subjects) — Higher elevations offer better odds than surrounding lowlands.

Moderate / Mixed 
4. Areas immediately bordering the Urals (e.g., parts of Ufa, Perm, Ekaterinburg environs) — Higher than pure lowlands but expected to become soggy/partially flooded; strong refugee pressure. 
5. Some inland elevated plateaus or hills in Siberia (scattered higher spots away from major rivers) — Temporary staging possible but eventual need to migrate.

Most Unsafe 
6. European Russia lowlands / Central Federal District (Moscow and surrounding oblasts, Volga region lowlands) — Moscow will be fully inundated; survival requires leaving for Urals, Finland, or southern mountains well above ~650–675 ft. 
7. St. Petersburg and Northwest lowlands — Shift-hour tidal flooding + permanent inundation; residents advised to relocate to Finnish/Scandinavian highlands early. 
8. Siberian lowlands and marshlands (vast central and western Siberia) — Explicitly low land that will be swallowed within months; survivors must plan boat migration. 
9. Northern coastal lowlands (Arctic coast, Kola Peninsula low areas) — Flat terrain increases flood risk; head to highlands without delay. 1
0. Kamchatka lowlands / volcanic zones — Volcanic activity plus coastal exposure (higher ground better but not ideal).

Practical Takeaway from the Material
The Ural Mountains and eastern Russian highlands are the clear preferences. Most of the country’s populated lowlands (including Moscow) are expected to flood permanently after the shift. If not already near high ground, the advice is to prepare boats early and migrate with the rising waters while using familiar landmarks. Northern and western lowlands are particularly exposed.
